'''Affordable Al's Discount Hospital''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{in|FOTV}}.

==Background==
A private pre-War hospital, the six-storey Affordable Al's was advertised as offering advantageous prices, including "revolutionary treatments" for the [[New Plague]] at low rates, [[lobotomy|lobotomies]] at half price, and comprehensive weight loss programs (on top of other hospital services, such as emergency rooms and surgery). After the [[Great War]], the hospital was abandoned, with many patients left to die on the gurneys with no assistance.<ref name="fotv202">{{FOTV|2|2}}</ref>

Scavenged and damaged by centuries of neglect and the elements, it eventually became a nest for a swarm of [[Radscorpion (TV series)|radscorpions]].<ref name="fotv202"/>

==In the TV series==
===[[The Golden Rule]]===
[[Lucy MacCready|Lucy]] and [[The Ghoul]], on their way to [[Las Vegas]], investigate the hospital when they hear a [[Wounded woman|woman]] scream for help. Despite the Ghoul's insistence, she enters the hospital, with the Ghoul reluctantly following along with [[CX404]]. Exploring the derelict, skeleton-strewn building they locate the woman and a [[wounded man]] in the basement kitchen. While Lucy tends to the woman, the Ghoul kills the man after recognizing them both as respectively a [[Legion]] slave and a legionary. The commotion attracts the attention of the radscorpions, leading to a fight in which both the woman and the Ghoul are struck and poisoned by the giant radscorpion. Lucy decides to treat the woman with her only stimpak, leaving the Ghoul to slowly regenerate under CX404's watch.<ref name="fotv202"/>

===[[The Profligate]]===
Inside the ruins of the hospital, [[the Ghoul]] has managed to crawl into a pool venue, still suffering the effects of the [[Radscorpion (TV series)|radscorpion]] sting that incapacitated him. With [[CX404|Dogmeat]] beside him for company, he takes out a [[skinning knife]] and extracts the stinger tip that was left inside his thigh from the creature's attack.

==Appearances==
Affordable Al's Discount Hospital appears only {{In|FOTV}} [[Fallout TV series episodes|episode]] "[[The Golden Rule]]."

[[Cassandra Hawthorne]] (pre-War) |headquarters =[[Los Angeles]] campus |parent =[[Vault-Tec Corporation]] (pre-War) |related =[[Vault 4]] }} '''Hawthorne Medical Laboratories''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== Founded in the pre-[[Great War|War]] era, Hawthorne Medical Laboratories was a subsidiary of the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]]. Its main campus in [[Los Angeles]], [[State#California|California]] was connected to the structure of [[Vault 4]], which was designed as a research facility to be overseen by HML leaders [[Lloyd Hawthorne|Lloyd]] and [[Cassandra Hawthorne]]. The exterior entrance of Vault 4 was built not far from the Hawthorne Medical Laboratories campus, with the two locations in visible distance of each other. To aid in the [[radiation]] and genetics experiments of the Vault's head researchers, the surface-level building was altered such that a hallway just inside from the main entrance was turned into a booby-trapped chamber, luring people in by using a fake door labeled as the entrance to a medical storage wing, then dropping them down a chute into a decontamination room within Vault 4 where they would be processed as new test subjects. ==In the TV series== ===[[The Past]]=== Due to [[Maximus]]' health declining from a wound he sustained during the ambush by fiends [[Javin]] and [[Rink]], [[Lucy MacLean|Lucy]] helps him search for medical supplies. They eventually reach the grounds of Hawthorne Medical Laboratories, though do not notice the signage marking it as a Vault-Tec property. After Lucy fails to re-emerge from scouting ahead, Maximus enters himself and is caught in the booby trap that brings him and Lucy into Vault 4.Events of {{FOTV|1|6}} ===[[The Radio]]=== After being exiled from Vault 4 over Lucy's transgressing into Level 12 and Maximus' unwitting attack on the peaceful Vault dwellers trying to rescue her, she convinces him to make slight amends by returning the fusion core he took from their reactor to power his [[T-60 power armor (TV series)|T-60 power armor]]. The two briefly return to the medical campus to deposit the core through the trapdoor, where it's found by a Vault janitor who indirectly thanks them.Events of {{FOTV|1|7}} Before leaving, Maximus opens up to Lucy, revealing his true name and that he allowed the real [[Titus|Knight Titus]] to die; Lucy forgives him and admits to some of her own crimes (as she sees them) during her wasteland journey. She extends a heartfelt welcome to join her in [[Vault 33]] after they rescue [[Hank MacLean|her father]] from [[Lee Moldaver|Moldaver]], to which he agrees as they depart to find [[Cold fusion|the artifact]] taken by [[Thaddeus]]. ==Appearances== Hawthorne Medical Laboratories appears {{In|FOTV}} [[Fallout TV series episodes|episodes]] "[[The Past]]" and "[[The Radio]]." ==Behind the scenes== * Pre-release images showing the name of Hawthorne Medical Laboratories were leaked to the public by u/PrinceDaCat on Reddit. * Scenes set at the Hawthorne Medical Laboratories campus were filmed at [[wikipedia:Bayley Seton Hospital|Bayley Seton Hospital]] in [[wikipedia:Staten Island|Staten Island, New York]]. ==Gallery== FOTV Hawthorne recreated_no_bottom.png|Hawthorne Medical Laboratories logo FOTV Hawthorne Logo.png|Full version of the van livery FOTV Hawthorne Medical Laboratories 2.png|Aerial view of the campus FOTV Hawthorne Medical Laboratories 3.png|[[Maximus]] explores the Hawthorne lobby FOTV Hawthorne Medical Labs Vault 4.png|Hawthorne Medical Laboratories; Vault 4 surface entrance visible in the distance Vault 4 entrance.jpg|Vault 4's surface entrance; the Hawthorne Medical Laboratories are visible to the left in the distance ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Fallout TV series}} [[Category:Fallout TV series mentioned-only organizations]] [[Category:Vault-Tec Corporation]] [[Category:Pre-War companies]] [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]] [[de:Hawthorne Medical Laboratories]] [[ru:Медицинские лаборатории Хоторна]]

The '''yao guai cave''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] in the [[Wilds]] in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]].

==Background==
As indicated by the "Hazardous Waste" signage outside and the presence of waste barrels and old equipment within, the natural cave formation was used as a disposal site for nuclear waste before the [[Great War]].

Sometime prior to [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]], a [[Yao guai (TV series)|yao guai]] claimed the cave as its nest. It preyed on surrounding wildlife and even several wastelanders with their bones and gory remains left strewn around inside.

==In the TV series==
===[[The Target]]===
Sometime after escaping from the [[Enclave research colony]], [[Siggi Wilzig]] and his companion [[CX404]] passed through the Wilds and came to a rest outside the cave. While Wilzig had a trail ration of [[Cram]], the canine wandered into the cave where it retrieved a severed human hand to bring back to its master. Wilzig realized the danger they were in as he then heard the distant roars of the yao guai prowling nearby, forcing a quick exit.

Later on, [[Knights of San Fernando|Brotherhood]] [[Titus|Knight Titus]] and his squire [[Maximus]] arrived in the area of the Wilds close to the cave by [[Vertibird (TV series)|vertibird]], after disembarking because Titus wanted "something to shoot at." They found Wilzig's abandoned campsite and evidence of his presence. Titus points out the cave and they suspect their target was taken by whatever lives inside it. The [[T-60 power armor (TV series)|T60-outfitted]] knight forces his squire to walk ahead of him as they look through the cave. However, they are unaware when the yao guai returns, leading to Titus being disarmed of his [[Heavy assault rifle (TV series)|heavy assault rifle]] when it attacks him. When Maximus fails to attack on his order, he runs in terror but is taken down by the creature and lethally mauled before the squire can kill it.

Titus demands Maximus heal him with a stimpak, but continues to verbally abuse him and threaten him for his failure, leading to Maximus condemning the knight and letting him succumb to his wounds. Maximus takes Titus' uniform and his T-60 power armor to impersonate him and leaves to complete the mission to find the artifact alone.

==Appearances==
The yao guai cave appears only in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]].

==Behind the scenes==
Scenes taking place at the yao guai cave were filmed at the [[wikipedia:Widow Jane Mine|Widow Jane Mine]] in [[wikipedia:Rosendale, New York|Rosendale, New York]].

Hollywood Boulevard:
{{Infobox location |games =FOTV |type = |image =FOTV Official Trailer Still 034.png |part of =[[Hollywood]], [[Boneyard|Los Angeles]] |creatures =[[Gulper (TV series)|Gulper]]
[[Deer]]
[[Leech]] }} '''Hollywood Boulevard''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{in|FOTV}}. ==Background== In the era before the [[Great War]], Hollywood Boulevard was famous as a cultural icon of the [[Hollywood]] district of [[Los Angeles]], [[State#California|California]], running through many tourist areas. Museums, landmarks, and more defined its attraction. After the bombs struck, a large part of the boulevard located off of Exit 12A from a nearby highway became submerged and surrounded by overgrown forests, with the concrete skeletons of old, stripped buildings still popping out of the water; by [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]], several have collapsed and sunk below the surface. A population of [[deer]] is present in the area, preyed upon by other creatures inhabiting the flooded areas, such as [[leech]]es. By 2296, the flooded area had become home to at least one [[Gulper (TV series)|gulper]], mutant creatures originally created by [[radiation]] experiments in [[Vault 4]]'s Level 12 laboratory, some of which evidently managed to escape from the Vault at some point after the [[Great War]].As seen in {{FOTV|1|7}} ==In the TV series== ===[[The Head]]=== While carrying the decapitated head of [[Siggi Wilzig]] on her solo trek to find [[Lee Moldaver|Moldaver]], [[Lucy MacLean]] reaches the flooded shores of the Boulevard where she is briefly amazed by the peripheral view of the area, then spots a baby deer drinking by the lakeside. She tries to feed it some grass and admire the peaceful atmosphere until a gulper strikes fast from the lake, dragging the deer into the water from behind a thicket of tall grass and forcing Lucy to equip her [[Tranq gun (TV series)|tranq gun]].Events of {{FOTV|1|3}} The gulper reemerges and catches Lucy off-guard, using its tongue to latch onto her backpack trying to drag her into the water too. Lucy manages to stun it by firing a tranq dart into the gulper's mouth. However, as the creature retreats, it catches the cloth sack holding the head, tearing it away as it returns to the depths. Pursuing the creature to the opposite side of the boulevard, Lucy listens as her [[Pip-Boy 3000 Mark V|Pip-Boy]]'s [[geiger counter]] starts to go off at detecting the intense radiation in the water. She remembers the tracker she implanted into the head and uses her Pip-Boy to track its location and prepares to go after it. However, she is interrupted by the arrival of [[the Ghoul]] following [[CX404]] who tracked Wilzig's scent to the Boulevard. After striking Lucy with his [[Dom Pedro (TV series weapon)|revolver]], the bounty hunter demands to know where the head is. When Lucy does not answer, he ransacks her backpack but does not find it. Though Lucy tries to tell him that she lost the head, the Ghoul, upon examining a nearby pile of animal droppings, deduces that the creature that attacked her and took the head is a gulper. Taking Lucy prisoner, the Ghoul ties up the Vault dweller and secures her to an old shipyard winch with an attached anchor. Lucy attempts to plead and strike a deal with the Ghoul, but he ignores her and starts dunking her into the irradiated waters, causing her geiger counter to go off again. Lucy frustratedly questions why he is torturing her, but the Ghoul elaborates that he is not interested in torture, rather merely using her as bait to attract the gulper and retrieve the head, then drops her in one more time. Eventually, Lucy's struggling makes enough noise to lure over the gulper, which bites down on the winch anchor to drag her deeper. The Ghoul manages to work the winch's controls and pull Lucy back along with the gulper onto the dock. While the gulper is trying to eat Lucy, the Ghoul attacks it with a harpoon but is pushed back. After it clamps down on her leg, taking off her boot, Lucy grabs the Ghoul's satchel and throws it into the gulper's mouth as a distraction, along with CX404 landing a bite on one of its limbs. The gulper spits out the satchel and retreats into the water, taking the head with it. Once the Ghoul recovers, he inspects his satchel and discovers that the gulper managed to destroy the tin containing his supply of [[inhaler vial]]s. In anger, he takes Lucy prisoner again, tying a rope leash onto the Vault dweller in order to take her to trade for more vials at the [[Super Duper Mart (TV series)|Super Duper Mart]]. Lucy again tries to beg with him, citing the Golden Rule, but the Ghoul callously replies that the wasteland has its own Golden Rule: "Thou shalt get sidetracked by bullshit every goddamn time." Lucy notices they are leaving CX404 behind at the waterside, but the Ghoul brushes it off stating the dog is not his. Sometime after Lucy and the Ghoul departed from the Boulevard, [[Thaddeus]] and [[Maximus]] (disguised as [[Titus|Knight Titus]]) arrive there following the radiation signature of the Ghoul, trying to locate the head themselves. When the tracker leads them into the waters of the flooded area, Thaddeus realizes the signature is not coming from the Ghoul but something else. The two then spot the gulper surfing through the water towards them. Maximus-as-Titus orders Thaddeus back to shore as he attempts to shoot the creature with his [[T60 pistol (TV series)|T60 pistol]] but to no effect. As the knight is confronted by the gulper emerging from the water, Thaddeus distracts it with a shot from a [[Heavy assault rifle (TV series)|heavy assault rifle]], but this causes it to charge toward him instead, managing to get his legs in its mouth. As the gulper tries to devour Thaddeus, Maximus runs after him and manages to stop the squire from being swallowed whole. Using the loose anchor caught in its mouth as a foothold, with a battlecry of "Ad victoriam!", Maximus extracts Thaddeus from the gulper's mouth and in the process pulls out a large portion of its innards, killing it. The two share a brief moment thanking the other for their help, then notice CX404 nearby licking at the head regurgitated by the gulper. Once they confirm it to be the object of their mission, they cheer in celebration and later depart from the Boulevard with their find. ==Behind the scenes== * The location of Hollywood Boulevard is based on the [[wikipedia:Hollywood Boulevard|real-world street of the same name]], which runs through Hollywood, Los Angeles. The highway exit marked on the Hollywood Boulevard road sign in the TV series, Exit 12A, is likewise a real-world freeway junction in Los Angeles, connecting Highway 101 with Lankershim Boulevard. ** A pre-release promotional image from the [[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|first season's Amazon overview page]] depicted the Hollywood Boulevard area from the TV series, but with the exit sign reading "Lankershim Boulevard" instead of Hollywood Boulevard. * Scenes taking place at Hollywood Boulevard was filmed at the [https://www.townofcortlandt.com/cn/webpage.cfm?tpid=18195 Cortlandt Quarry] in [[wikipedia:Verplanck, New York|Verplanck, New York]], situated at the northwesternmost lake within hamlet limits. Another location within Westchester County, Briarcliff Manor, was also used for scenes taking place at [[Hollywood Hills]] in the [[The End (episode)|first episode]].[https://archive.ph/Szq8p Visit Westchester County NY: Filmed in Westchester (archived)] ==Gallery== Fallout Season 1 Amazon CX404 bg.jpg|Pre-release promotional image from the [[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 1 Amazon overview page]], showing the sign's original design reading "Lankershim Boulevard" ==References== {{References}} '''Meta''' {{References|group=Meta}} {{Navbox Fallout TV series}} [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]] [[Category:Roadways]]

The '''Hollywood Walk of Fame''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}.

==Background==
A pre-[[Great War|War]] landmark erected in the namesake district of [[Hollywood]] in [[Los Angeles]], [[State#California|California]], it served as a major tourist attraction for years. The walk passed by major film studios in Hollywood, including the site of [[California Crest Studios]].

By the late 23rd century, the desert winds and rolling sands of the [[wasteland]] have resulted in much of it being buried and illegible.

[[Lucy MacLean]] and [[the Ghoul]] walk along a section of the sand-covered landmark during the trek from [[Hollywood Boulevard]] to a [[Super Duper Mart (TV series)|Super Duper Mart]] near [[Santa Monica Boulevard]].

==Appearances==

'''Los Angeles City Hall''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]] {{in|FOTV}}.

==Background==
Prior to the [[Great War]], Los Angeles City Hall acted as the center of government for the city of Los Angeles, California. In the late 2070s, the city hall was the site of a union protest against [[RobCo Industries]] during the [[automation riots]].<ref>{{FOTV|2|1}}: Opening scene. When the union protestors are seen, the building they are at can be briefly seen to have the words "City Hall" written on it.</ref>

==Appearances==
Los Angeles City Hall appears in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]].
{{FOTV appearances|9=201}}

==Behind the scenes==
Los Angeles City Hall is based on the real-world [[Wikipedia:Los Angeles City Hall|Los Angeles City Hall]], which was constructed in 1928. Apart from the large structure at the back, Los Angeles City Hall appears largely the same.

'''Shady Sands Elementary School''' is a building in [[Shady Sands]], appearing briefly {{in|FOTV}}. 

==Background==
A four-story building in downtown Shady Sands, down the street from the [[Shady Sands civic center|civic center]], the school educated the youngest minds of the Republic's capital. Laid out like classic pre-War schools, with lockers belonging to students lining the walls and filled with their books and other items, the school also had a separate playground out the front door for the youngest. On top of being served by the capital's mass transit system, it also had a working school bus.<ref>{{fotv|1|5}}</ref>

'''Los Angeles International Airport'''{{Ref|(Note)}} was a pre-[[Great War|War]] [[airport]] located in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]] which appears {{in|FOTV}}.

==Background==
The airport survived the Great War mostly intact and is still a monumental landmark in the desert wastelands of California as of [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]]. Many [[aircraft]] crashed around the airport and its surrounding terrain during the Great War. Airplane parts have also been scavenged and/or salvaged for settlements such as [[Filly]]. At some point, a [[Soviet satellite|satellite]] owned by the [[Soviet Union]] also crashed near the airport. There was a [[donut shop]] located along a road not far from the airport.

In 2296, [[Lucy MacLean]] and [[Siggi Wilzig]] passed by the airport after escaping from Filly, en route to deliver Wilzig to [[Lee Moldaver]] at [[Griffith Observatory]]. Wilzig ultimately died nearby at the crashed Soviet satellite. Others tracking Wilzig (first [[the Ghoul]] and Wilzig's former dog [[CX404]], then [[Maximus]] and [[Thaddeus]] of the [[Brotherhood of Steel]]) would also pass by the area later.

==Notes==
* The airport is also prominently shown in the ending credits of "[[The Target]]," which depicts it as housing a fleet of [[Vertibird]]s, with numerous crashed and/or grounded airplanes shown around, as well as a billboard advertising [[Horizon Airlines]]. Two corpses in power armor are also seen, along with a poster of Uncle Sam modified to advertise the Brotherhood of Steel.

==Appearances==
The Los Angeles airport appears only {{in|FOTV}}, in the episodes "[[The Target]]" and "[[The Head]]." It also appears in a pre-War flashback in the episode "[[The Innovator]]."

==Behind the scenes==
* [[wikipedia:Los Angeles International Airport|Los Angeles International Airport]] is a real-world airport in Los Angeles, California. The large arch-like building in the middle of the airport is based on the real-world [[wikipedia:Theme Building|Theme Building]], built at the airport between 1957 and 1961.
** {{Note|(Note)}} No name has been given for this location in-universe, other than the audio narration for the ending credits of "[[The Target]]" identifying it as an airport, although it has been called LAX in news articles.<ref name="indiewire">[https://archive.ph/NeZIR ''Indiewire'': "'Fallout' Builds a World Unlike Any Other — Including the Video Game"]: ''"Los Angeles touchstones like the Capitol Records building, LAX, and Randy's Donuts were created digitally to anchor the viewer in the city."''</ref><ref>[https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/awards/story/2024-06-11/fallout-production-design-uses-new-york-coastal-africa ''Los Angeles Times'': "In 'Fallout,' a destroyed L.A. comes to life, with some help from... Namibia?"]: ''"Worth's team provided the broken-arch remains of LAX's Theme Building with a giant, eaten-away Randy's Donuts nearby for the show's lead wanderers — Lucy, walking nightmare the Ghoul (Walton Goggins) and Maximus (Aaron Moten), a renegade from the fascistic Brotherhood of Steel — to pass by from various distances and directions."''</ref> The airport's real-world name is therefore used for this article.
* The airport was filmed entirely using digital effects.<ref name="indiewire" />

[[Shopkeep Simon]] (ostensibly) }} '''Sonny's Sundries''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{in|FOTV}}. ==Background== A general store within [[Freeside]], Sonny's Sundries sold various items including sundries, weapons, medicine, and other equipment. It was owned and operated by [[Sonny]] up until July [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]], when Sonny was murdered by a thief named [[Shopkeep Simon|Simon]]. Simon subsequently took over, pretending to be the shopkeeper by putting on Sonny's clothes, which were far too small for him, and heavily inflating Sonny's prices.{{FOTV|2|6}} Sonny's remains were shoved into a garbage bin inside near the back of the store. ==In the TV series== ===[[The Wrangler]]=== Suffering from a [[Buffout addiction]], [[Lucy MacLean]] is given [[bottle cap]]s by [[the Ghoul]], who tells her to go to Sonny's Sundries to purchase [[Addictol (TV series)|Addictol]] with which to clean out her system. When she reaches the store, she sees that the price for Addictol, written on a chalkboard outside the main door, has been raised to a degree that she cannot afford. Lucy is disheartened, but sees a back door left open on the side of the shop, and decides that to deal with her present circumstances she must steal a vial of Addictol from the store. Sneaking in, she finds the medicine, takes it, and pauses to inspect and additionally take a [[Power fist (TV series)|power fist]] on display, as well as a bag to hold it. While she does so, she notices a dead and bloody body stuffed into a nearby trash can—that of Sonny, though Lucy is initially unaware of this. While distracted, Shopkeep Simon sees her and confronts her, and Lucy tries to assuage the man and come across as a regular shopper. As she does so, she notices a portrait of the store owner, the dead man in the trash can. She inquires about the dead body, which Simon unconvincingly claims was an attempted thief. Lucy questions him why the man is naked, which causes Simon to defensively claim that naked robbers aren't unusual. She questions him further about why his clothes don't fit and deduces the body in the trash can is the original shopkeeper, pulling her 10mm pistol on Simon. She tries to avoid further escalation but doesn't hesitate to shoot Simon as he immediately reaches for a weapon. Lucy inspects him, finding she had shot him dead and starts reconsidering her recent actions, taking the Addictol and power fist and leaving soon after a [[Freeside customer|customer]] arrives to find her standing over Simon's corpse. Afterwards, Lucy administers the Addictol to herself outside the store, causing her to vomit horribly. ==Appearances== Sonny's Sundries appears only {{In|FOTV}} [[Fallout TV series episodes|episode]] "[[The Wrangler]]." ==Gallery== Fallout Season 2 Amazon Freeside bg.jpg|Bottom right, seen on [[Fallout season 2 Amazon overview|season 2 overview on Prime Video]] FTV_S2E5_Still_106.png|[[Lucy MacLean]] swipes a [[Power fist (TV series)|power fist]] FTV_S2E5_Still_107.png|Lucy tries to hide ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Fallout TV series}} [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]] [[Category:Freeside buildings]] [[ru:Всячина Сонни]]

'''Ma June's Sundries''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}.

==Background==
Owned and operated by the namesake [[Ma June]] for some time prior to [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]], the general goods store serves as a mainstay of the trading town of [[Filly]] in [[New California]]. In addition to various bits and bobs including old [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]] products and merchandise, June also keeps a selection of weapons behind the store counter for sale including [[Plasma pistol (TV series)|plasma pistols]], a [[Junk Jet (TV series)|Junk Jet]], [[Laser musket (TV series)|laser muskets]], etc. Due to the collapse of the [[New California Republic]]'s economy around the greater [[Los Angeles]] area following the destruction of [[Shady Sands]] in 2283, stores like Ma June's returned to the tried-and-true barter system utilizing [[bottle cap]]s with a prohibition on refunds.<ref>As seen in the {{FOTV|1|2}}</ref>

==''Fallout'' TV series==
===[[The Target]]===
[[Lucy MacLean|Lucy]] enters Ma June's Sundries and, at first, comments about how Ma June was selling Vault-Tec items and surmises that she must do business with criminals. Aside from Lucy's interest in a [[Lee Moldaver|particular criminal]], Ma June was more interested in the fact that Lucy was a [[Vault]] dweller and tried to call on her roommate [[Barv]]. As Lucy tries to ask Ma June about the criminal she is looking for, while Ma June beckons Barv, Lucy alerts Ma June when she drops Moldaver's name.

After closing [[Ma June's ledger|her ledger]] and telling Barv to return to her room, Ma June then debates Lucy about her Vault naivete, who begs Ma June for any information on Moldaver. In the end, Ma June kicks Lucy out of her store, but as Lucy leaves, she runs into [[Siggi Wilzig]], who she met at her campfire the other night in front of the store.

The two would briefly talk until Ma June walked out of her store. After confirming Wilzig's identity, she told him to enter her store and demanded that Lucy scram. However, [[the Ghoul]], who sat on a chair close by to the store, accosts Wilzig, blows off his left foot, and in retaliation, Ma June puts a bounty on the Ghoul's head.

During the shootout between the Ghoul and the [[Filly townsperson|Filly townsfolk]] hoping to cash in on the bounty on the Ghoul's head. Lucy looked at Ma June's finance book and saw that Lee Moldavor's name was written in the book. She then confronts the Ghoul in front of the store and attempts to reason with him until [[Maximus]] appears inside a [[T-60 power armor]]. As Maximus distracted the Ghoul by fighting him, Lucy and Ma June carried Wilzig into the store's backroom, where Ma June demanded that Barv fetch a new leg. Though Barv complains that she was trying to eat her [[Pork n' Beans#Greasy Prospector Pork n' Beans|beans]], she still agrees to do it.

As Ma June tries to get Wilzig comfortable on a chair with his leg up on the table, Barv eventually arrives with a [[Jim's Limbs]] crate, and Ma June uses one of them on his blown-off foot. Once it was agreed that Lucy would transport Wilzig to Moldaver and Ma June input Moldaver's coordinates into her [[Pip-Boy]], the two left through the back door.

Afterward, the Ghoul entered Ma June's Sundries, where he spots a puddle of blood and a box of Jim's Limbs. Walking outside, the Ghoul finds the wounded CX404; he then takes CX404 into Ma June's Sundries and uses a [[Stimpak (TV series)|stimpak]] on her, which revives her.

===[[The Beginning]]===
It is unknown if Ma June returned to her shop and continued business following the Ghoul's massacre. By a later point in 2296, the town of Filly is taken over by the [[Brotherhood of Steel]], with the store in particular converted into an armory stockpiling their weaponry.

'''Santa Monica''' was a pre-War city in [[Los Angeles]] County, [[California]] which appears {{in|FOTV}}.

==Background==
Before the Great War, Santa Monica was a famous tourist destination mostly for the [[Santa Monica Pier]], which is largely still standing by [[Timeline#2296|2296]]. It was also the home to [[Vault 33]], which was constructed just south of the Santa Monica Pier in a bunker-like building along the coast.

==Appearances==
Santa Monica appears in the ''[[Fallout (TV series)|Fallout]]'' television series, although the area corresponding to it is visible on the [[Fallout map|first ''Fallout'' game's world map]] as well.

==Behind the scenes==
The Santa Monica Pier was filmed at [[wikipedia:Elizabeth Bay|Elizabeth Bay, Namibia]], a ghost town and former diamond mine. Visual effects were used to add the pier's Ferris wheel and roller coaster, as well as the Malibu Mountains in the background, but everything else in the shots was practical.<ref>[https://archive.ph/A5p5K Los Angeles Times: "In ‘Fallout,’ a destroyed L.A. comes to life, with some help from ... Namibia?"]</ref>

[[Enclave]] (financing) }} The '''Las Vegas management Vault'''{{Ref|(Note 1)}} is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] in [[Fallout TV series season 2|season 2]] of the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]]. ==Background== This facility was one of a series of special vaults for management employees of the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] to oversee the other mainline Vaults.[[Barb Howard]]: ''"I have worked hard to make sure we go into a special vault for management, where we will oversee all of the other vaults."''
({{FOTV|1|6}}) It was one of many such facilities, along with one built somewhere in [[Oregon]] and another somewhere in [[California]].[[Lucy MacLean]]: ''"I'd ask why my dad ran into a den of giant monsters, but you'd probably just tell me to shut the fudge up."''
[[The Ghoul]]: ''"[sighs] Before the war, there was a plan... for a special Vault. A Vault for management. That's where my wife is. Where my daughter is, too."''
Lucy MacLean: ''"You never found it?"''
The Ghoul: ''"Oh no, I found one, in California. It was empty. Found another one in Oregon. It was empty, too. Turns out, there's more than a few special Vaults for management sprinkled across the Wasteland. All of 'em empty. But I've never found one in Vegas."''
Lucy MacLean: ''"So, you think if my dad's in there, maybe your wife and daughter are, too?"''
The Ghoul: ''"Uh-huh. And now, they're surrounded by these fuckin' things."''
({{FOTV|2|5}}) While officially a Vault-Tec facility, it was secretly constructed for their financiers, the [[Enclave]]. The facility was built half a mile underneath [[New Vegas|Las Vegas]], [[Nevada]], accessible from the [[Lucky 38]] via a series of subterranean tunnels. [[Robert House]], who was aware that nuclear war was inevitable and took steps to preserve Las Vegas from the bombs, permitted Vault-Tec to build this vault, but then "rigged" it in some way to make sure the company could not use it for their plans.[[Robert House]]: ''"Vault-Tec wanted an impenetrable Vault buried half a mile below the city, but I was always one step ahead."''
[[The Ghoul]]: ''"Uh-huh."''
House: ''"I rigged every aspect of the city so I could protect its future. I rigged every slot machine, every roulette wheel. Turn left. I even rigged their impenetrable Vault for management."''
The Ghoul: ''"Is that so?"''
House: ''"But I miscalculated. Because this Vault belongs not to Vault-Tec but to their investors. I never fathomed there could be someone one step ahead of me. Until I saw your demon in the snow. [...] When it came to predicting the end of the world, I was off by just a smidge. But when it came to controlling the future, I was wholly outclassed by an invisible adversary. It was they who set the Deathclaws on Vegas. And now one of their acolytes is here, in this very building. [...] The Enclave's eyes are everywhere. You should know, Mr. Howard. Two hundred years ago, you delivered that diode into their possession yourself. You helped bring forth the greatest threat to the Wasteland. You were their unwitting servant."''
({{FOTV|2|8}}) {{Small|Robert House confirms that the deathclaw in Alaska as seen in "The Demon in the Snow" was released by the Enclave.}} It is not specified what House did, but he is shown to have control over at least some of the management Vault's systems through his mainframe.{{FOTV|2|8}}: Robert House is able to guide the Ghoul directly into the management Vault and also opens his wife's and daughter's cryo pods for him, indicating that he is familiar with the Vault and its systems. At the Las Vegas management vault, research was undertaken on the [[brain-computer interface chip|Black Box chip]] technology developed by House, which he had licensed to Vault-Tec in exchange for ownership of their [[Cold fusion|cold fusion diode]].{{FOTV|2|6}} The management Vault's researchers specifically worked on miniaturizing the chip's hardware while maintaining its functionality,[[Hank MacLean]]: ''"Uh, I've been keeping busy. I'm in Vegas these days, back in your old stomping grounds, actually… trying to pick up where you all left off. Looks like a couple of the Vault experiments ran into some speed bumps. 24 made progress on the brain-computer interface. This one, miniaturization. What it all needs is integrating. But I'm confident that if I just roll up my sleeves, I can bring it all home for you. Then, we can finally talk about my promotion. [blows sharply] I'm gonna complete the work you started. And when this is all over, you will be begging me to help you."''
({{FOTV|2|1}}) with experiments on live test subjects including both mice and humans. However, they evidently were not able to overcome the technology's flaw of causing subjects' heads to overload and explode when receiving more complex commands. Other areas of the facility included a communications room equipped with ham radio technology, as well as three separate sections containing [[cryonics]] facilities: one suite specifically for Vault-Tec management staff, and the "Premium Elite Plus" suite for private individuals (though the cost of a single ticket was noted to be significantly expensive) to be kept preserved until [[Reclamation Day (event)|Reclamation Day]]. [[Barb Howard]], a Vault-Tec senior executive, had a spot within the management cryonics bay, as did her daughter [[Janey Howard|Janey]]. The third preserved animal test subjects. At least one of these cryo pods was put to use by the time that the [[Great War]] struck in October 2077, with their occupants remaining preserved for the centuries that followed. However, the facility itself was left abandoned, and had remained that way for a very long time by 2296, with only a few of the Black Box chip test subjects' remains still present as signs of former life. At some point, Barb Howard's cryo pod was opened, and a postcard was left inside, seemingly a message from Barb herself to her husband as a clue for where to find them after the war. ===Use by Hank MacLean=== After his escape from [[Griffith Observatory]] in the midst of [[Battle of Griffith Observatory|the attack]] by the [[Knights of San Fernando]] against [[Lee Moldaver]]'s [[New California Republic|NCR]] remnant group,{{FOTV|1|8}} disgraced [[Vault 33]] overseer [[Hank MacLean]] fled [[New California]] on a long trek wearing a stolen set of Brotherhood [[T-60 power armor (TV series)|T-60 power armor]] in order to reach the facility, located underneath the [[Lucky 38]] casino in the ruins of [[New Vegas]]. Before getting there, he made a detour to [[Vault 24]] to acquire the hard drive containing the Vault's research data regarding their experiments to enhance the black box chip, bringing it with him for the remainder of his trek. Once there he continued the experiments in mind-control technology, exhausting the animal test-subjects, and later delving into humans left in their cryo-pods before abducting wastelanders before he could perfect the technology. He planned to wipe out the factions warring on the surface like the NCR and Legion, though he was ultimately thwarted by his daughter Lucy. However he had dispatched mind-controlled agents to enact portions of his plan that he kept secret before erasing his own memories. ==In the TV series== ===[[The Innovator]]=== Around the same time that Hank's daughter [[Lucy MacLean|Lucy]] and [[the Ghoul]] had followed his trail to Vault 24, Hank himself made it into the subterranean Vault-Tec facility. In a room with many desks, he starts up a [[terminal]] and logs into the system, confirming he still retained access to the network. After cleaning up and picking out new work attire, Hank locates the "Global Comms" room and uses the radio console to reach out to an unknown recipient. He says to them that he intends to continue the facility staff's experiments with miniaturizing the chip and combining it with Vault 24's data to perfect the design, all in an effort to curry a "promotion" that he believes will have them "begging [him] to help." ===[[The Golden Rule]]=== Once he locates the facility's cryogenic repository of experimental white mice, Hank starts with his experiments to improve the black box technology. However, this leads to several failures as the signal's increased strength kills the test subjects too quickly to get meaningful results, but Hank resolves to continue anyway, making multiple trips to and from the cryonic repository. Eventually, though, his experimental progress stalls due to the mice dying too quickly, so he explores more of the complex. He ultimately finds his way to the "Premium Elite Plus" suite where Hank thaws out one of them, a man named [[Stephen Winthrop]]. The confused Steve is attached with a black box chip by Hank as he wonders if he was brought out because of Reclamation Day; Hank claims that it is, but not as Vault-Tec planned. As Hank prepares Steve for his current experiment, he remarks about his preference for "the classics" and how much has changed in the world. Steve becomes more aware of his helpless state as Hank reveals that he did not include his family in the program, which Steve claims was because it was too expensive to buy more than one ticket. Hank emphasizes how a commitment to family builds a civilization, then compares it to his experiments, claiming that through enhancing the black box, he will also improve a piece of "outdated technology" — civilization. Steve begins to react to the black box's signal as Hank increases its strength, eventually resulting in his explosive death; Hank coldly remarks "if at first you don't succeed... try, try again." ===[[The Wrangler]]=== Now with his experiments transitioning into human testing, Hank decides to "recruit" from outside the facility. His search brings him to an [[abandoned taco stand]] where he finds the [[snake oil salesman]] on a "date" with [[Fisto]], wherein he knocks the salesman out with a crowbar and transports him back to the facility. The salesman later awakens to find himself in Hank's workstation, restrained to a table with a black box chip implanted in his neck. Hank asks if he would like to forget every memory he has ever had, including people he had met and details about his life, while retaining the use of his language and motor skills; the salesman eagerly agrees. Hank then uses a machine to remove the memories from his brain. At first, the salesman seems pleased and even aroused but then begins to wince seemingly in pain and scream as Hank turns up the dial. Unlike with Stephen Winthrop, the salesman's head does not explode, and the procedure proves to be a success. As he looks over the docile salesman, Hank relishes the results of his experiments finally achieving progress and presses a button on his console to begin the next stage of his plan. At some point during his tests, Hank learned that Lucy had made it to New Vegas to hunt him down. He dispatched the mind-controlled salesman as his representative to strike a deal with the Ghoul to have his daughter returned to Vault 33 while he completed his plans. Evidently suspecting that something would go awry, Hank came to the surface in person, finding Lucy collapsed on the floor of her room in the [[Atomic Wrangler Casino]] shortly after she launched the Ghoul out the window for betraying her. He comforts his daughter as she falls unconscious from a tranquilizer and later transports her to the facility. ===[[The Other Player]]=== In the following morning, Lucy wakes up inside a room of the facility which has been made to resemble a domestic bedroom. Sneaking outside, she notices two [[Legionary (TV series)|legionaries]] walking down a hall towards her room, and attempts to ambush them, but is taken aback when they greet her cheerfully as if nothing is wrong. Continuing to investigate, Lucy discovers the room with many desks, which is now occupied many [[X-Branch office worker|office workers]] in matching attire, who barely acknowledge Lucy's presence and simply work cheerfully among themselves to produce more of the black box chips. Lucy continues further past and finally finds her father preparing food in a simulation room dressed up as a kitchen and dining room. Though Lucy is on her guard, Hank seems completely unfazed to see her, and attempts to win her over to his side by deriding the seeming pointlessness of the factional violence on the surface. Unconvinced, Lucy threatens Hank with a pair of scissors and tells him she is taking him back to Vault 33 to face justice; Hank handcuffs himself and seemingly surrenders, leaving with Lucy. When the two return to the room with many desks, the office workers are shocked to see Hank being threatened, and all eyes turn on Hank and Lucy. Hank reassures them that everything is fine; he claims to Lucy that he has been using the black box chips to give new, peaceful lives to people on the surface who were formerly murderers or otherwise locked in violent conflict. Lucy does not buy his argument that this is benevolent and tries to tell the brainwashed workers they are free, but they refuse to leave, believing the facility is safer for them than the surface. Hank suggests that he and Lucy will simply leave the entrances to the facility open once they leave so that the workers can make their own choice on whether to stay. As Lucy prepares to take him away, Hank instead has her remain there as he opens up a door leading to an elevator, which he calls a "management perk." Just then, the brainwashed snake oil salesman and another worker wheel in [[Biff (TV series)|Ranger Biff]] and a [[massive legionary]], both of whom have been captured and tied to chairs. They have been implanted with black box chips, but the chips have not yet been activated, and the salesman asks Hank for permission. Hank defers to Lucy, and she refuses, telling them to let the two men go. However, the massive legionary is untied first and immediately begins trying to attack Biff for being a member of the NCR. Lucy tries to protect Biff but is ultimately unable to stop the legionary from repeatedly attacking Biff with a stapler. With no one else intervening, and Hank presenting the black box chips as the only way to save Biff, Lucy is convinced to activate the two men's chips, immediately rendering them docile and friendly towards each other as they leave to treat Biff's wounds. ===[[The Handoff]]=== Reflecting on the scene that just occurred and noticing the snake oil salesman standing by blankly, Lucy asks Hank about the black box chips, which he states are configured to give people selective degrees of amnesia, which can then be replaced with preset memories. Lucy continues to view this as wrong and asks Hank how she can stop him; he claims that the people who have already been chipped cannot be returned to their original state, but that Lucy can prevent him from creating more chips if she destroys the mainframe that controls all of the chips. He leads her towards the room with the mainframe, allowing her to drive the golf cart. Just outside the door to the mainframe room, Lucy is distracted from her goal by a worker behind them who says that the floor is wet due to his mopping; Lucy realizes that this worker was the massive legionary, now rendered completely harmless. This causes her to falter and become swayed by Hank's arguments, believing that the chips can be used to pacify Caesar's Legion and prevent them from harming anyone else in the Mojave. Hank, continuing to try and sway Lucy to his side, has the two of them eat mashed potatoes in the simulation dining room. Lucy seems to be fine at first, but when she sees that Biff is serving them, now no longer remembering anything about his past life with the NCR or even having previously met Lucy a week ago, she turns against Hank for good. Hank dismisses Biff and tells Lucy his opinion that the NCR and the Legion are equally problematic, pointing to the NCR's taxes and imperialism before burning his hand when taking a pie out of the oven. Lucy, still feigning support, pretends to be freeing Hank from his handcuffs, but instead cuffs him to the oven, revealing that she is aware he was manipulating her the whole time. She leaves to destroy the mainframe while Hank loses his cool. Lucy drives the golf cart, shakily, down the halls towards the mainframe room, passing by the comms room but failing to hear her brother [[Norm MacLean|Norm]] transmit his own message asking Lucy for help and calling out their father for hiding the true nature of Vault 33 from them. She opens the mainframe room, crowbar in hand, but is shocked to see that the mainframe is actually a severed head (that of pre-War [[United States Congress|U.S. Congresswoman]] [[Diane Welch]], though Lucy does not know this) attached to a neural interface helmet. ===[[The Strip]]=== {{section|FOTV}} ==Appearances== The Las Vegas management Vault appears only in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]]. ==Behind the scenes== * {{Note|(Note 1)}} This is a descriptive title, as no official name for the facility has been confirmed, though the Ghoul calls it a special "Vault for management." Some characters later seen inside the facility are credited as "X-Branch office workers."{{FOTV|2|6}}: Two of the mind-controlled wastelanders seen in the facility are credited as being "X-Branch office workers." In behind the scenes materials and interviews, the facility (or at least the parts of it seen in the show) has been called the "X-Branch" or "Site X."[https://archive.ph/HGQ3K Art of VFX: "Fallout – Season 2: Vincent Poitras – VFX Supervisor – Raynault VFX"] * According to lead VFX artist Jay Worth, the exterior of the tower structure seen inside the Vault was filmed at the Wrapper Building in Culver City. He stated he and his team chose the building because of its unique structure, then added additional details in post-production, including pipes and bridges.[https://www.atlasobscura.com/places/the-wrapper-los-angeles-california Atlas Obscura: The (W)rapper, Los Angeles, California] ==Gallery== FTV S2E8 Still 092.png ===Concept art=== FOTV DJennings Int X-Branch Storage Room.jpg FOTV DJennings Int X-Branch Storage Room 04.jpg FOTV DJennings Int X-Branch Storage Room 09.jpg FOTV DJennings Int X-Branch Storage Room 10.jpg ===Behind the scenes=== FOTV DJennings X-Branch Door.jpg FOTV DJennings X-Branch Storage Room Set.jpg FOTV DJennings X-Branch Storage Room Set 2.jpg FOTV DJennings X-Branch Storage Room Set 3.jpg FOTV DJennings X-Branch Storage Room Set 4.jpg ==References== {{References}} '''Meta''' {{References|group="Meta"}} {{Stub|FOTV}} {{Navbox Fallout TV series}} [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]] [[Category:Vault-Tec locations]] [[ru:Специальное убежище «Волт-Тек»]]

{{Infobox location |games =FNV,FOTV |type =Building |image =The Kings.jpg |map marker image =King's School of Impersonation map.png |part of =[[Freeside]] |factions =[[Kings]] |leaders =[[The King]] |merchants =[[Sergio]] (barber) |robots =[[Rex (Fallout: New Vegas)|Rex]] |quests =[[G.I. Blues]]
[[Kings' Gambit]]
[[Nothin' But a Hound Dog]] |cell name =FreesideKingsHouse (interior) |refid ={{ID|10e03b}} (interior) }} {{Quotation|Oh, I know it says "school" out front, but everything in here seems to be related to the worship of [[Elvis Presley|some guy]] from back in the day.|[[The King]]|sound=FNV_TheKing_SchoolOutFront.ogg}} The '''King's School of Impersonation''' is an [[Fallout: New Vegas locations#Freeside|unmarked location]] within [[Freeside]] in the [[Mojave Wasteland]] {{In|FNV}}. It also appears in [[Fallout TV series season 2|season 2]] of {{in|FOTV|noin}}. ==Background== Prior to the [[Great War]], the building was host to an [[Elvis Presley]] impersonation school that served the greater Las Vegas area. It included the use of holotapes and outfits to teach how to mimic his voice and fashion as well as a classroom curriculum that taught how to replicate his speech patterns and catchphrases, and even what kind of foods he liked to eat.The [[Courier]]: ''"Is that what you guys do, pretend to be this guy?"''
The King: ''"Somethin' like that, yeah. There were some working tapes here when we first got here, so we know what he sounded like. Sadly, they stopped working a few years back, so I sold them to a junk merchant who was passing through, otherwise I'd play some for you. All the outfits you see my guy wearing around were originally found in here, too. Along with more hair gel than you can shake a stick at.
([[VFSTheKing.txt|The King's dialogue]]) Following the nuclear apocalypse, the building, like most of the area around Vegas was left to rot and ruin until [[Timeline#2274|2274]], when [[Robert House|Mr. House]] emerged from the [[Lucky 38]] with his [[Securitron]]s to establish [[New Vegas]] ahead of the arrival of the [[New California Republic]]. He issued an ultimatum to the [[tribals]] and raiders living in the ruins, ultimately recruiting those who became the [[Three Families]] while the rest were either evicted or killed. One of the tribal groups tried to eke out a living in the slums but found firsthand how rough living could be. They eventually came across the King's School of Impersonation and learned about the image and ideals of one called "the King" (they never learned his real name as all evidence had been unintelligbly degraded). Inspired, the tribals reinvented themselves as the [[Kings]], led by [[The King]], based around the anarchic ideal of complete personal freedom, where "every man is a king in [their] own right."The [[Courier]]: ''"Tell me about the Kings."''
The King: ''"We're different than other gangs, and not just because we dress better. We're not just a group of thugs looking for our next fight. The Kings are about an idea, you see? Where every man is free to follow his own path, do his own thing. Where every man is a king in his own right."''
([[VFSTheKing.txt|The King's dialogue]]) ==Layout== Situated southeast of the [[Atomic Wrangler Casino]] in the south section of Freeside, the building interior is sizable and consists of three floors. All items in the building are considered owned and in taking them, [[Karma (Fallout: New Vegas)|Karma]] will be lost. The sole exception are the beds which can be freely used to [[Resting|sleep]]. It can be entered through a door on the northmost corner of the building into a reception area. ===First floor=== In the reception room, couches line the wall, [[Empty whiskey bottle (Fallout: New Vegas)|empty whiskey bottle]]s litter the floor, and Kings gang members mill about the room, sitting on barstools around a semicircle countertop. An inoperable coffee machine sits on the counter and a broken freezer behind contains [[empty Sunset Sarsaparilla bottle]]s. There are two directions to proceed from the reception area. To the left of the counter is the entrance to a theater of sorts, with a stage, spotlights, and seating. [[Pacer]] will stop the Courier upon approach, requiring payment of 50 or 500 caps to speak with The King. The Courier can offer 5 caps, which he will refuse unless a 60 Speech check is passed, or pay no caps by passing the initial 60 Speech check. No matter what amount is given to Pacer, if the Courier tells The King, he will reimburse the player character and have unique comments on each differing sum. Inside the stage room, a Kings gang member performs for The King, who sits in front of the stage joined by his [[Cyberdog (Fallout: New Vegas)|cyberdog]], [[Rex (Fallout: New Vegas)|Rex]]. A locked door on the southside of the stage room can only be opened with [[The King's key]], obtainable only by pickpocketing. The area behind the door is accessible immediately by following the hallways of the first floor, and therefore pickpocketing the key is unnecessary to explore the building in full. The second way to proceed from the reception area is a door directly opposite the main entrance. It leads to the living areas of the building, of which there are three floors. Each floor contains bedrooms, recreation rooms, and storage areas. Rooms on the first floor include a storage closet full of wire music stands, and two bathrooms. There are three bedrooms containing nine total beds and two dressing rooms on the first floor. In one of the rooms, cups alongside three [[ping pong ball]]s are set up as if to play beer pong. In one of the dressing rooms, [[Sergio]] can be found. He is the gang's hairstylist. If the Courier becomes a member of the gang, they can change their hairstyle here. The staircase to the second floor is located in the west corner. ===Second floor=== The second floor has two bathrooms that are larger than those on the preceding floor. The lefthand bathroom has three stalls and two sinks, while the righthand stall has two stalls, two urinals, and one sink. All of the water in these bathrooms is radiation-free. In the righthand bathroom, a [[straight razor]] can be found on the edge of the sink with a pool of blood on the floor, presumably from a botched shaving attempt. A [[First aid box (Fallout: New Vegas)|first aid box]] is mounted on the wall in each bathroom. Apart from the bathrooms, this floor is comprised entirely of bedrooms. There are six bedrooms containing 21 beds on the second floor. The bedrooms have various personal effects within, including [[Switchblade (Fallout: New Vegas)|switchblades]], [[Cherry bomb (Fallout: New Vegas)|cherry bombs]], and alcohol bottles. One bedroom has a battery-powered light on the ground next to [[Scrap metal (Fallout: New Vegas)|scrap metal]], a [[Hammer (Fallout: New Vegas)|hammer]], and a [[Wrench (Fallout: New Vegas)|wrench]]. Another bedroom has a [[Chessboard (Fallout: New Vegas)|chessboard]] propped up on cinderblocks. A bedroom in the north corner has a mattress lying on a desk, with a bottle of [[Wine (Fallout: New Vegas)|wine]] balanced on top. The Kings have turned another bedroom into a putting green, lining up squares of carpet underneath a cup on its side, with four [[Golf ball (Fallout: New Vegas)|golf balls]] and a [[9 iron]]. The staircase to the third floor is located in the south corner of the building. ===Third floor=== By proceeding in a clockwise fashion, the Courier will first find Pacer's bedroom, with a lit cigar on the end table next to a queen-sized bed. This bed will grant the Courier the [[Well Rested]] effect, as will the other beds on the third floor. The next room is a storage room filled with desks. To the right of the storage room is the bedroom of The King. A Kings member stands guard outside. The bedroom is large, with windows extending to the top of the tall, coffered ceiling. Looking at the building from outside, the third-floor windows on the recessed walls above the main entrance belong to this room. The bedroom is occupied by two [[King groupie]]s wearing [[Sexy sleepwear (Fallout: New Vegas)|sexy sleepwear]]. They cannot be engaged in dialogue but will say various things about The King or ask if the Courier is supposed to be there. The room has a unique heart-shaped bed, a [[Fallout 3 and New Vegas miscellaneous world objects#Pool table|pool table]], [[Jukebox (Fallout: New Vegas)|jukebox]], and a [[Sunset Sarsaparilla vending machine (Fallout: New Vegas)|Sunset Sarsaparilla vending machine]]. The King can be found sitting in the chair next to the jukebox at times, next to Rex, behind a table with a ''[[Boxing Times]]'' skill magazine and [[Harmonica (Fallout: New Vegas)|harmonica]]. Connected to The King's bedroom is the bedroom belonging to the groupies, fitted with two queen-sized beds, a vanity, and a bathtub. The last room on the third floor is filled with clothing items, including [[Kings outfit]]s and [[Jailhouse Rocker (Fallout: New Vegas)|Jailhouse Rocker]]s. If the Courier joins the gang, they will be given an outfit of their own. There is a large chalkboard on the wall with faint writing. Upon closer inspection, the Courier can read a "King Impersonation Checklist" with instructions to "move hips," "say 'uh huh'," "say momma," and "peanut butter & banana sandwiches" as well as "This week's homework" including "(illegible) girls (illegible)," "gyrate," and "aint nothin but a hound dog" written across the bottom. Other chalkboards can be found throughout the building featuring similar scribbles, including "make $$$." The hallway leads back to the stairway in the south corner. ==Notable loot== * 32 [[Kings outfit]]s and three [[Jailhouse Rocker (Fallout: New Vegas)|Jailhouse Rocker]]s - On the third floor. * Three [[ping pong ball]]s - In a first-floor bedroom. * [[Figaro]] - a unique variant of the [[straight razor]], carried by [[Sergio]]. * [[Viva Las Vegas]] - Carried by [[The King]]. * Four [[Golf ball (Fallout: New Vegas)|golf balls]] - In a second-floor bedroom along with a [[9 iron]]. ==Related quests== * [[G.I. Blues]] * [[Kings' Gambit]] * [[Nothin' But a Hound Dog]] ==Notes== The location of the King's School of Impersonation differs in the ''Fallout'' TV series compared to ''Fallout: New Vegas''. In the game, the store is situated near the beginning of the south-central part of Freeside, while in the show, it is one of the last buildings on the right before reaching [[The Strip North Gate]]. It is also shown as being directly across the street from [[Mick & Ralph's]], which also changed position in the show compared to the game. ==Appearances== The King's School of Impersonation appears {{In|FNV}} and {{in|FOTV|noin}}. ==Behind the scenes== The in-game King's School of Impersonation is based on the real-world location of [[wikipedia:Four Queens|Four Queens Hotel and Casino]], located in the [[wikipedia:Fremont Street Experience|Fremont Street Experience]] in [[wikipedia:Las Vegas|Las Vegas, Nevada]]. The Ghoul's grave:
{{Infobox location |games =FOTV |factions =[[Dom Pedro (character)|Dom Pedro's]] gang }} '''The Ghoul's grave''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== At some point, [[the Ghoul]] was captured by a powerful man known as [[Dom Pedro (character)|Dom Pedro]] and brought to his stronghold. Considering the Ghoul a personal enemy,In Scene 46 of "The End," mariachi music is heard playing in the scene depicting a guard with the attire and facial hair traditionally associated with Mexican banditos and revolutionaries. The sign at the location reads "CEMENTERIO. ENEMIGOS DE DOM PEDRO," which is Spanish for "Cemetery. Enemies of Dom Pedro." Dom Pedro had the gunslinger buried alive in a grave, sustained only by an IV drip. It's said that Dom Pedro would dig up the Ghoul annually to cut off pieces of his body before reburial.[[Slim (TV series)|Slim]]: ''"How do we know which grave?"''
[[Honcho]]: ''"Well, Slim, we look for the fresh one. Dom Pedro has our friend dug up once a year. Cuts some pieces off and puts him right back in the ground."''
({{FOTV|1|1}}) ==In the TV series== ===[[The End (episode)|The End]]=== Sometime in 2296, a group of bounty hunters consisting of [[Honcho]], [[Biggie]], and [[Slim (TV series)|Slim]] snuck into Dom Pedro's fortress at night, with Biggie using his [[Junk Jet (TV series)|Junk Jet]] to take out [[Dom Pedro's guard|a guard]].{{FOTV|1|1}} Honcho then explains that they are searching for a notorious bounty hunter whom Dom Pedro has held captive for several years. They eventually come upon a small graveyard, which includes one grave with a pair of IV bags and tubes emerging from the dirt. Biggie and Slim are shocked to realize the person they are looking for is a [[ghoul]], and Honcho says that his father once worked with him.[[Slim (TV series)|Slim]]: ''"Shit. You're telling me this supreme badass we're looking for is a godforsaken mutant?"''
[[Honcho]]: ''"Have some respec'. That's your prospective coworker you's talking about and our ticket to a big payoff."''
Slim: ''"Thought you said you knew this guy."''
Honcho: ''"I said I knew of him. My pop worked with him once."''
({{FOTV|1|1}}) Biggie expresses concern that he may have gone [[Feral ghoul|feral]]. Honcho brings out a [[chicken]] and explains that a feral ghoul cannot tolerate them. The hunters dig up the coffin contained in the grave and place the chicken in front of it before opening it up. From inside, the Ghoul emerges, revealed to be an aged and mutated Cooper Howard. He playfully picks up the chicken, terrifying Biggie and Slim. Honcho proposes they work together to secure a large bounty. He elaborates that [[Siggi Wilzig|the target]] has gone to seek out [[Lee Moldaver|Moldaver]] in California, specifying that he knows the Ghoul is originally from there. The Ghoul takes offense to the mention of his past and claims that, unlike them, he pursues bounties "for the love of the game." The Ghoul proceeds to kill Slim and Biggie. He then wounds Honcho and drags him over to toss him into the coffin and let it drop back into the open grave, asserting that cowpokes like him "take it as it comes." The Ghoul spares the chicken, taking it with him as he leaves to pursue the bounty alone. ==Notes== The Ghoul's introduction of being buried alive in a grave is similar to [[Coffin Willie]], who was similarly buried alive in a grave in [[Golgotha]] near [[New Reno]] for years before being dug up by the [[Chosen One]] {{In|FO2}}. ==References== {{References}} [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]]

The Atomic Wrangler has you covered!|[[Atomic Wrangler crier]]|sound=NVAtomicWranglerCrierAtomicWranglerHasYouCovered.ogg}} The '''Atomic Wrangler Bar & Casino''', typically shortened to just the '''Atomic Wrangler''', is an [[Fallout: New Vegas locations#Freeside|unmarked location]] within [[Freeside]] in the [[Mojave Wasteland]] {{In|FNV}}. It also appears in [[Fallout TV series season 2|season 2]] of {{in|FOTV|noin}}.{{FOTV|2|5}} ==Background== {{Quotation|It's not much to look at, but if you can't afford to get into The Strip, the Atomic Wrangler's the best place to gamble in Freeside.|[[Fallout: New Vegas loading screens|''Fallout: New Vegas'' loading screen]]}} The Atomic Wrangler Bar & Casino was a pre-[[Great War|War]] nightclub located on [[Fremont Street]] in [[New Vegas|Las Vegas]], [[Nevada]], advertising itself as "the West's finest watering hole."[[:File:AtomicWranglerAdv.png|Atomic Wrangler billboard]] In 2077, it played host to a meeting between [[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]] and [[Diane Welch|Congresswoman Diane Welch]], who arranged for Howard to secretly meet with the [[Last President of the United States|U.S. president]] in order to give him the [[Cold fusion|cold fusion diode]] Howard had stolen from [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]].{{FOTV|2|7}} By [[Timeline#2281|2281]], the Atomic Wrangler is the only active [[Fallout: New Vegas casinos|casino]] in the slum community of Freeside,[[:File:FNV Atomic Wrangler card.png|Vault playing card]] also doubling as a flophouse, brothel, and prominent source of the [[chems]] craze in the area. Its owners and operators are the Garret twins, [[James Garret|James]] and [[Francine Garret|Francine]], who keep a staff of armed thugs for protection and provide service even to members of the [[Van Graffs]] in the nearby [[Silver Rush]] and the [[Kings]] from the down-the-street [[King's School of Impersonation]]. Many caravaneers and poor (but not impoverished) [[New California Republic|NCR]] folks can also be found here when they lack deep enough pockets to make it to the [[New Vegas Strip|Strip]].[[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition Tour of the Mojave Wasteland#2C.06 Atomic Wrangler Casino|''Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition'' Tour of the Mojave Wasteland; 2C.06 Atomic Wrangler Casino]] As of 2296, the Atomic Wrangler continues to operate in Freeside, though by then, the barkeep is a man named [[Shotgun Jeff]] and it is unclear whether the Garret twins are still involved with the establishment. ==Layout== ===''Fallout: New Vegas''=== Situated in the south end of Freeside, the Wrangler can be seen past the patched-together "Freeside" sign on the west side with itself featuring a neon sign of a futuristic cowboy riding a stylized atom. ====Bottom level==== The main room has a vaulted ceiling, a stage, and a bar. The room directly opposite the entrance features the casino's [[Atomic Wrangler cashier|cashier]] and casino games. The cashier's room contains some [[Pre-War money (Fallout: New Vegas)|pre-War money]] and [[Fallout: New Vegas consumables|chems]] in the safes. To the right are the bathrooms and a staircase to the second story balconies. Behind the bar is a kitchen and storeroom, accessible via a door around the corner near the bathroom with a Very Hard lock. Both of the Garrets have the [[Fallout: New Vegas keys#Atomic Wrangler upstairs key|key]] to the room, but it will eventually become unlocked as soon as one of the Garrets head upstairs to their room, as they neglect to relock it. The storage room/kitchen area behind the bar contains a significant amount of common items of moderate value, such as various alcoholic beverages. The Courier can also find a large number of [[Fresh apple (Fallout: New Vegas)|fresh apples]], [[Fresh pear (Fallout: New Vegas)|pears]], and [[Fresh carrot (Fallout: New Vegas)|carrots]] (at least a half-dozen each), as well as a weapons locker and medicine locker, both containing many useful items. ====Second level==== This level has a balcony that oversees the stage and bar. Off of the balcony are four rooms. A rentable room is located in the eastern corner of the second floor. Stairways lead back down or up to the third level. ====Corner room==== {{main|Atomic Wrangler corner room}} On the second level, there is a door that leads to the corner room, which can be gained as [[Fallout: New Vegas player character housing|player housing]] after completing [[Debt Collector]] for Francine. ====Third level==== This level is where the employees, including the Garret twins, live. In the employee living area, four guards can be found either milling around or sleeping. The door to this level is secured with an Average lock or opened with the key held by the Garrets. Guards here will not be hostile initially, instead following the Courier around, repeating a warning to leave. Rooms include a large bedroom the Garret twins take turns sleeping in, two general sleeping areas for employees (one containing 8 beds and one with 6 beds), two bathrooms and a storage room. Guard sleeping areas have [[Footlocker (Fallout: New Vegas)|footlockers]] with minor loot. The two bathrooms contain [[First aid box (Fallout: New Vegas)|first aid box]]es. The storage room, located to the right of the sleeping area, is filled with file cabinets, metal crates, and a gun cabinet. ===''Fallout'' TV series=== The Atomic Wrangler, as depicted in the TV series, has both similarities to and differences from its portrayal in ''Fallout: New Vegas''. The casino storefront is still located across from the [[Silver Rush]], except down at the end of a main street with multiple other stores including [[Sonny's Sundries]]. The bottom floor is widely different from its previous appearance, with glass double doors instead of one door, no visible evidence of a performance stage, and the second floor balcony extending above the bar. The staircase itself is also relocated into a curved form opposite from the bar instead of behind it. What's shown of the upper floors consists mostly of a single hotel room which has an attached bathroom and open windows looking out into Freeside. ==Gambling== [[File:TheAtomicWrangler.jpg|thumb|220px|The gambling tables]] ; Games * The Atomic Wrangler offers [[Blackjack]], [[Roulette]], and [[Slots]]. * The Atomic Wrangler pays 6:5 on blackjack, and the dealer must draw to 16. ; Rewards and Ban As the player earns chips, the casino offers increasingly valuable gifts: * 1,250+ chips: [[Beer (Fallout: New Vegas)|beer]] * 2,500+ chips: [[Whiskey (Fallout: New Vegas)|whiskey]] and dapper gambler hat * 3,750+ chips: [[absinthe]], [[Rum & Nuka]] & [[dapper gambler suit]] * 5000+ chips: banned from gambling. After the player character earns 5,000+ chips, they will be banned from playing games in the Atomic Wrangler Casino. They can still use its other functions, such as the bar and services of the prostitutes (if [[Wang Dang Atomic Tango]] has been completed), but they cannot win any more money, permanently. If the player character breaks the house limit before getting any comp gifts (by getting a large win) they will not receive any comps they have missed. There is no floor manager at this casino, so the comp gifts are awarded directly to the player character upon reaching each winning milestone. Play is still interrupted by the player character being forced out of whichever game they were playing to receive the message rewarding their earned comps. ==Inhabitants== * [[Atomic Wrangler cashier]] * [[Atomic Wrangler guard]] * [[Caleb McCaffery]] (before completing Debt Collector) * [[Francine Garret]] * [[Hadrian (Fallout: New Vegas)|Hadrian]] (before completing Talent Pool) * [[Henry Jamison]] * [[James Garret]] * [[Beatrix Russell]] (after completing Wang Dang Atomic Tango) * [[Fisto (character)|Fisto]] (after completing Wang Dang Atomic Tango) * [[Santiago (Fallout: New Vegas)|Santiago]] or [[Old Ben]] (after completing Wang Dang Atomic Tango) ==Notable loot== * [[Nuka-Cola Victory (Fallout: New Vegas)|Nuka-Cola Victory]] - On the third level in the Garrets' room, on a shelf. ==Related quests== {{columns|2| * [[Debt Collector]] * [[Talent Pool]] * [[Wang Dang Atomic Tango]] * ''[[Big Winner, Atomic Wrangler]]'' * ''[[Friend of the Followers]]'' * ''[[Long-Term Care]]'' * ''[[Smooth-Talking Criminal]]'' }} ==Notes== * The casino's [[Atomic Wrangler crier|crier]] can be found outside on the street corner below the "Freeside" sign, advertising the casino to the public. * Despite the Wrangler's reputation as a free-swinging brothel, dialogue options with Francine Garret that would suggest the same, and sex noises coming through the walls of most rooms, there are no prostitutes in the casino beyond ones the player character recruits during Wang Dang Atomic Tango. After finishing the quest, one can then have sex with either ghoul cowgirl/dominatrix Beatrix Russell, Santiago/Old Ben (depending on decisions during the quest), or the sex-bot Fisto. * Like all other casinos in the game, the amount of money kept in the cashier's office is small. Robbing the cashier nets at random a few dozen bundles of pre-War money and approximately 100 [[Bottle cap (Fallout: New Vegas)|caps]]. The [[Fallout: New Vegas keys#Atomic Wrangler bank key|Atomic Wrangler bank key]] is carried by both Garret twins. * Exiting from dialogue with Fisto will give 10 [[Bottle cap (Fallout: New Vegas)|caps]], which can be repeated ad infinitum. * Being banned from the casino by gambling does not affect the progress of completing the [[The Courier Who Broke the Bank]] achievement/trophy. * The casino also appears in ''[[Fallout 76]]'' as a [[Fallout 76 shelters|shelter]] purchasable in the [[Atomic Shop]]. In-game it has a similar layout to its initial appearance though is larger than it appeared in ''Fallout: New Vegas''. ==Behind the scenes== ;''Fallout: New Vegas'' * The in-game Atomic Wrangler Casino is based on the real-world Atomic Liquors store, located on [[wikipedia:Fremont Street|Fremont Street]] in downtown Las Vegas. * The logo of the Atomic Wrangler is a reference to a scene in the film ''[[Wikipedia:Dr. Strangelove|Dr. Strangelove]]'' in which Major T. J. "King" Kong rides a falling nuclear bomb like a rodeo cowboy. * Area designer [[Robert Lee]], who was one of three designers on Freeside, wrote for characters within this location and designed the quests [[Wang Dang Atomic Tango]] and [[Debt Collector]].[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E4zN5Qy3Izo Freeside's Cut Content] ;''Fallout'' TV series * In season 2 of the TV series, Freeside and the exterior of the Atomic Wrangler were filmed at [[wikipedia:Movie ranch#Monogram Ranch/Melody Ranch|Melody Ranch Motion Picture Studio]] in [[wikipedia:Santa Clarita, California|Santa Clarita, California]]. This '''Starlight Drive-in Theatre''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] in the [[Mojave Wasteland]] in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]].

==Background==
This small drive-in theater, operated by [[Starlight Theaters]], was located somewhere on the outskirts of [[New Vegas|Las Vegas]], [[Nevada]]. By the time of the [[Great War]], the theater was offering a double feature showing of ''[[A Man and His Dog|A Man and His Dog 3]]'' at 6:30 PM and another film involving Dracula later in the night.<ref>[[:File:FOTV S2E1 Starlight Drive-in Theatre.png|Theater marquee]]</ref>

The theater was also used as the site of [[Vault 24]], the entrance of which was hidden behind the movie screen.

==In the TV series==
===[[The Innovator]]===
[[Lucy MacLean|Lucy]] and [[the Ghoul]] come across the theater during their journey to [[New Vegas]], following in the tracks of [[Hank MacLean]]. While the Ghoul is initially drawn to the theater marquee, as it listed one of his old movies (''A Man and His Dog 3''), Lucy's attention is immediately caught by the open door of Vault 24 behind the tattered movie screen. They soon enter the Vault to follow Hank, who did the same thing.

==Appearances==
The Starlight Drive-in Theatre appears only in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]].
