{{Infobox location |games =FOTV |type = |image =FOTV Griffith Observatory.png |image desc =Appearance {{In|FOTV}} |part of =[[Boneyard|Los Angeles]] |local map = |factions =[[New California Republic]] (2283 - 2296) |owners =[[Vault-Tec Corporation]] (pre-War) }} '''Griffith Observatory''' is a post-[[Great War|War]] settlement and [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{in|FOTV}}. ==Background== Prior to the [[Great War]], Griffith Observatory was sponsored by the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] and designated as a "Science & Friendship Center."{{FOTV|1|7}}: Seen on a billboard in the credits sequence. The observatory was able to survive the devastation caused by the nuclear strikes on [[Los Angeles]], although it suffered some structural damage along with wear and tear over the following 200 years. Around [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2283|2283]], a nuclear bomb destroyed the [[New California Republic]] capital of [[Shady Sands]]. The NCR presence in Los Angeles subsequently declined; however, surviving NCR forces who were not in Shady Sands when it was destroyed coalesced under the leadership of [[Lee Moldaver]],[[Norm MacLean]]: ''"So you met my sister?"''
[[Ma June]]: ''"Yeah, back in Filly. Before the Brotherhood of Steel burnt it down. Had her help a fella from the Enclave get through the Shithole to some folks from the NCR who weren't in town when Shady Sands blew up. Pretty slim odds. What with it being Khan country."''
({{FOTV|2|5}}) a pre-War scientist and notable figure in Shady Sands prior to its destruction. She led them to garrison the old observatory, which became the last known remaining NCR headquarters in Los Angeles, housing both [[NCR citizen (TV series)|civilians]] and [[NCR soldier (TV series)|NCR soldiers]]. There, she hoped to restore the ruined Shady Sands' prospects by building a [[cold fusion]] reactor using technology she herself had created over 200 years ago. However, the reactor required two essential components: the first was a cold fusion diode, and the second were the credentials of a pre-War Vault-Tec employee. The credentials were needed to activate the reactor inside the observatory, as the cold fusion technology had become proprietary to Vault-Tec before the Great War. In [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]], Moldaver acted to obtain both components. She and her [[Moldaver's elite guard|elite guard]] led a gang of [[Vault 32 raider|raiders]] to infiltrate the [[Three Vaults]] under [[Santa Monica]], masquerading as residents of [[Vault 32]] to enter [[Vault 33]] during their Triennial Trade ceremony. In their subsequent attack, they were are able to capture 33's overseer [[Hank MacLean]] and escape with him as their prisoner after the raiders massacred many of the Vault dwellers, bringing him to the observatory.Events of {{FOTV|1|1}} The goal of this was to have Hank relinquish his Vault-Tec executive credentials in order to unlock the encryption on the cold fusion reactor. To obtain the cold fusion diode itself, Moldaver got in contact with [[Siggi Wilzig]], a member of the [[Enclave]] who had possession of it, and made arrangements for him to come to her at the observatory to deliver the technological artifact. In response to her father's abduction by Moldaver, [[Lucy MacLean]] set out into the wasteland to find and rescue him, later being given coordinates to the observatory from [[Ma June]], who had been paid to assist Wilzig's own arrival there. Interference by [[the Ghoul]] and Brotherhood of Steel ends up forcing Lucy to instead take the severed head of Wilzig containing the cold fusion artifact to trade for her father's life.Events of {{FOTV|1|2}} She was eventually able to arrive at the observatory, where she met Moldaver, who then obtained the diode from Lucy and the codes from Hank. However, the observatory was attacked by the [[Brotherhood of Steel]] chapter known as the [[Knights of San Fernando]] just before the reactor could be activated. In the [[Battle of Griffith Observatory|ensuing battle]], the NCR forces at the observatory were routed, with Moldaver herself dying just after activating the reactor, which successfully restored power to much of the Los Angeles ruins. The Knights of San Fernando subsequently seized the cold fusion technology and took it with them to [[Area 51]] for their own purposes.Events of {{FOTV|2|2}} It is unclear whether any faction still holds the observatory after this battle. ==In the TV series== ===[[The End (episode)|The End]]=== Griffith Observatory is briefly seen at the start of the episode, as the Great War strikes and nuclear explosions occur in Los Angeles. ===[[The Beginning]]=== By [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]], Lucy reaches the walls of the observatory with the cargo of Wilzig's head and is brought to Moldaver, noticing many NCR citizens being sheltered there, including a [[freed ghoul|ghoul she freed]] from the [[Super Duper Mart (TV series)|Super Duper Mart]] organ harvesters. Upon meeting Moldaver in her headquarters atop the observatory's dome, she attempts to negotiate giving the head and the artifact in exchange for the imprisoned Hank, but Moldaver takes the opportunity to explain the reason why she came to Vault 33 and took her father in the first place, revealing his role in the destruction of Shady Sands including killing thousands of NCR citzens along with turning her mother, [[Rose MacLean|Rose]] into a [[ghoul]]. Lucy's heartbreak over the truth about her father compels Hank to follow Moldaver's orders, inputting his credentials to unlock the cold fusion technology and begin the reactor's power-up.Events of {{FOTV|1|8}} Shortly after, however, the military forces of the Brotherhood arrive and start [[Battle of Griffith Observatory|a battle]] to eradicate the NCR forces and secure control of the reactor. Moldaver attempts to lead her troops in defense of the observatory but the Brotherhood's firepower allows them to plow through the defenders with some casualties. The Ghoul, having also reached the observatory around this time, briefly sets back the Brotherhood's advance when he uses his knowledge of the [[T-60 power armor (TV series)|T-60 power armor]]'s vulnerability to slaughter one of their squads. Hank escapes after being confronted by the Ghoul, and the Ghoul and Lucy leave to track him down. A fatally wounded Moldaver returns to the dome to complete the activation of the cold fusion reactor, dying in her chair while warning Maximus of what could happen if the Brotherhood is allowed to take control of cold fusion. Other Brotherhood forces barge in soon after and celebrate Maximus, assuming he had killed Moldaver. ==Layout== The observatory's outer area has been fortified with junk walls and old car wrecks manned by armed NCR guards to become the stronghold of the Flame Mother, Lee Moldaver. The towers of the observatory include anti-air missile launchers that were used during the Brotherhood assault, while some of the guards also wield man-portable rocket-launchers. The '''Sunset Sarsaparilla factory''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] in the [[Mojave Wasteland]] in [[Fallout TV series season 2|season 2]] of the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]].

==Background==
The factory was constructed by the [[Sunset Sarsaparilla Company]] on a hilltop elevated above and overlooking the city of [[New Vegas|Las Vegas]], [[Nevada]] and was neighbored by a motel business. What is shown of the present-day area indicates it survived the [[Great War]] intact with little, if any [[radiation]] affecting it.

At some point, a [[RobCo Industries|RobCo]] [[Securitron]] ended up at the factory for unknown reasons. By 2296, a combination of age and lack of maintenance resulted in its programming going haywire, causing it to erratically shift between thinking it was a masseuse and a security guard.

==In the TV series==
===[[The Profligate]]===
Sometime after escaping from the [[KPSS radio station]] near [[Hollywood Hills]],<ref>{{FOTV|1|7}}</ref> the [[Mutations|mutated]] ex-[[Knights of San Fernando|Brotherhood]] squire [[Thaddeus]] left [[New California]] and made his way to the [[Mojave Wasteland]] where he discovered the abandoned factory. His exploration included finding its [[Extremely broken Securitron|malfunctioning "security guard"]] which he chose to stay apart from but still keep around for protection. With his access to the bottling floor, Thaddeus decided to set up a [[Bottle cap|cap]] collecting operation; to maximize profit, he installed himself as floor manager and gathered a "crew" of orphaned [[human]] and [[ghoul]] children to man the conveyor belts bringing out crates of soda so they could pry off the caps while drinking the leftover soda for refreshment.

The quiet living Thaddeus was enjoying was eventually upended when the bottling factory was stormed by [[Maximus]] and [[Xander Harkness]] from the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 4)|Commonwealth Brotherhood]] after they detected the plant's power signature. They destroyed the Securitron and discovered the crew of children, which Xander wanted to eliminate the ghouls in accordance with the [[Codex]]. Thaddeus tried to intervene to protect them, but Xander's refusal to back down forced Maximus to kill him by driving a [[Super sledge (TV series)|super sledge]] into his head.

===[[The Demon in the Snow]]===
Shortly after killing Xander, Maximus tells Thaddeus he has to help him cover it up from the Brotherhood, right as a vertibird arrives that was tracking them. Despite initial reluctance and claiming he prefers to run away, Thaddeus agrees to help after Max points out the Brotherhood would discover the kids in the process of looking for him, killing the ghouls and recruiting the humans, if they did not create a distraction. Thaddeus takes Maximus's suit of T-60 power armor and disguises himself as the Commonwealth paladin as they are flown back to [[Area 51]].

==Notes==
It is never explicitly clarified if this location is meant to be the [[Sunset Sarsaparilla headquarters]] that appeared in ''[[Fallout: New Vegas]]''. Although they both have large statues depicting a [[Sunset Sarsaparilla]] bottle in the front of their buildings, the two locations have more differences than they do similarities. The TV series location appears to more closely resemble a factory or warehouse in its exterior, differing greatly from the headquarters building which was largely an office structure with an attached factory. The interior layout of the headquarters also appears to differ considerably from what is visible in the TV series location. The area surrounding the factory in the TV series has several differences as well, having more space outside the building, and being located in close proximity to a motel and hills, far away from the city of [[New Vegas]], whereas the headquarters in ''Fallout: New Vegas'' is situated within the edges of the western part of the city.

==Appearances==
The Sunset Sarsaparilla factory appears only in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]].

({{FOTV|1|6}}) After the Great War, the building was left abandoned, with the corpses of pre-War employees still strewn about. In 2296, following the destruction of [[Filly]] by the [[Knights of San Fernando]], former Filly residents [[Ma June]] and [[Barv]] moved into the lobby of the Vault-Tec headquarters, claiming it as their new squat and [[Radroach (TV series)|radroach]] farm. ==Layout== The Vault-Tec building is a large skyscraper designed in a Mid-Century Modern architectural style, located somewhere within Los Angeles. There is a parking lot in front of the main entrance, leading into a lobby with elevators adjacent to the reception desk. A conference room was at the back of the ground floor. Elsewhere in the building, there were a set of adjoining communications rooms. Barb Howard's office was in another space nearby. There was also a room, presumably adjacent to Barb's office, that was used as a waiting room by Cooper Howard when he visited to spy on his wife. Some rooms on other floors of the building are also seen. One floor includes another conference room adjacent to a working area with several desks and cubicles and the elevator hall nearby; this was the area used by Barb Howard for her meeting with (the body double of) Robert House regarding cold fusion. In another unknown area, there was a large, two-story meeting room with seats on a ledge overlooking the main circular conference table, with a holographic map of the U.S. behind them; this space was used by Barb and Bud Askins to host a secret meeting about the Vault experiments. One hallway in some area of the building, seen in the credits sequence of "[[The Other Player]]," was shown to include multiple Vault-Tec research areas. There were rooms for "Vault-Tec Agriculture R&D," "Vault-Tec Toilet R&D," "Door Engineering," "Water Chip R&D," as well as "[[Forced Evolutionary Virus|F.E.V. Cultivation]]." One end of this hall included a security checkpoint, guarded by a [[sentry bot]], leading into the highly restricted-access Human Resources R&D Department. The other end attached to a standard office space, at the end of which was the office of Bud Askins. Askins decorated his office with numerous posters of Cooper Howard's movies, as well as a [[Giddyup Buttercup]], ''[[Grognak the Barbarian]]'' comics and a figurine, and a [[Brain bot|Rollerbrain]] user manual. After the Great War, the building's entrance and windows, as well as the door to an adjacent hallway, are seen to have been boarded up by 2296. The lobby was painted with graffiti in some places, calling out Vault-Tec for being "liars." Corpses of some of the building's employees were still present, including the receptionist [[Janice (TV series)|Janice]], as well as the janitor and two others who seemingly committed suicide using [[Plan D]] pills. By July 2296, the lobby had been claimed by Ma June and Barv after they fled Filly. They boarded up the elevators, which they were using to hold radroaches for farming, and set the first floor conference room as an armory. ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===[[The Beginning]]=== Sometime in the early-to-mid 2070s, Barb was driven to the headquarters by her then-husband [[Cooper Howard]], where they also encountered Bud as Barb entered the building. Unbeknownst to either of them, Cooper had secretly planted a listening device given to him by [[Lee Moldaver|Kate Williams]] into Barb's [[Pip-Boy 3000 Mark V|Pip-Boy]] in order to confirm his suspicions that Vault-Tec was up to something shady. However, he realizes just after Barb entered the HQ that the device had a limited range, forcing him to trick his way into the building by convincing Barb's secretary [[Betty Pearson]] that he wanted to wait in her office. Meanwhile, Bud and Barb go to a private section of the building, containing a secure boardroom where they begin a meeting with various corporate moguls representing big companies like [[REPCONN Aerospace]], [[West Tek]], [[Big MT (company)|Big MT]], and [[RobCo Industries]].[https://gamerant.com/fallout-tv-show-vault-tec-pre-war-design ''Gamerant'' - "Fallout TV Show's Production Designer Talks Making Vault-Tec From the Ground Up"]Events of {{FOTV|1|8}} Unaware of Cooper's listening in, Bud discusses with the moguls about the progression of Project Safehouse, Vault-Tec's joint operation with the [[United States government]] to construct a vast series of subterranean fallout shelters known as [[Vault]]s as a proactive defense against nuclear war and offers potential avenues of collaboration with their various groups. After the meeting descends into bickering over Vault-Tec's methods, Barb, seemingly taking cues from a private message from a [[man in shadows]] watching the meeting from an elevated section, takes the reins and formally offers each of the moguls a selection of the over 100 vaults in the country for their own use. While the others begin brainstorming ideas for experiments to perform on their populations of test subjects, [[Robert House]] questions how Vault-Tec plans to ensure that the Vaults are actually used. To Cooper's shock, Barb openly suggests that the corporations orchestrate the nuclear apocalypse themselves to guarantee that theirs will be the only monopoly left after the dust and fallout clears. Cooper is left stunned by the revelation of his wife's heartlessness, such that he does not initially react to being introduced to one of Bud's junior managers, [[Hank MacLean|Henry "Hank" MacLean]] who wanted to meet him due to his fandom for Cooper's acting work. ===[[The Wrangler]]=== Around July 2296, [[Norm MacLean]] and a group of [[Vault 31 dweller]]s are led to the Vault-Tec headquarters by [[Ronnie McCurtry]] to enact phase two of the [[Bud's Buds]] project plan. By that time, the headquarters had been left abandoned, with the remains of its former employees still strewn about. Part of the first floor had been claimed by [[Ma June]] and [[Barv]], former residents of the junk town of [[Filly]] who were forced to relocate due to the [[Knights of San Fernando]] having burned down their town, and partially turned it into a radroach farm. ===[[The Strip]]=== During a struggle, [[Claudia (TV series)|Claudia]] inadvertently hits an elevator button, releasing a swarm of radroaches on the [[Vault 31 dweller]]s. Only Norm and an injured Claudia survive the attack and Norm takes Claudia away from the building in a cart. ==Notes== * A different [[Vault-Tec headquarters (Los Angeles)|Vault-Tec headquarters]] also in [[Los Angeles]] was mentioned in ''[[Fallout 2]]''. It is unclear whether these are meant to be the same location or separate ones, but the differences in these locations' appearances is intentional (see [[#Behind the scenes|below]]). * As seen in "The Beginning," the building is marked with signage for Vault-Tec Industries rather than the Vault-Tec Corporation. These two names have been used seemingly interchangeably for Vault-Tec throughout the ''Fallout'' series; the TV series has specifically only used "Vault-Tec Industries" so far. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quotation|The basement layer was based on Dr. Strangelove, the movie, with the light, roundtable, and cement room. It was fun to do. That was in the middle of Manhattan in a theater, so we had to use whatever we could to pull all that stuff together, because you know we shot in New York and also in Namibia and Utah, all to do LA.|[[Howard Cummings]]}} * For season 1, the exterior scenes of the Vault-Tec building were shot at [https://www.fordham.edu/graduate-school-of-social-service/about/campus-locations/westchester-campus/ Fordham University's Westchester Graduate School of Social Service], with the entire superstructure digitally added in post-processing. The site was chosen by Paul Kramer, a member of the film crew's location management team. It was selected due to its mid-century aesthetic, which the team wanted for pre-War Los Angeles; the structure of the building as seen in the TV series was based on the [[Vault-Tec Regional HQ]] found in [[Boston]] in ''[[Fallout 4]]'', but given a "West Coast architecture twist." ** According to [[Howard Cummings]], production designer on the TV series, it was intentional that the building was not a recreation of the "core LA Vault-Tec Headquarters" previously seen in ''Fallout 2'', due to his intention to have the pre-War scenes fit a "slicker" mid-century look. * The arrangement of the conference room is a deliberate reference to [https://pl.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plik:Dr._Strangelove_-_The_War_Room.png the war room] in the 1964 film ''Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb''. In the movie, the titular [[wikipedia:Dr._Strangelove|Dr. Merkwurdigliebe]] actually proposes the construction of nuclear shelters not dissimilar to Vaults in the event of Soviet nuclear aggression in the final act. Unlike the HQ building's exterior and suite shots, the conference scene was filmed in a Manhattan movie theater. ==Gallery== FOTV Vault-Tec Industries Building Top.png|Superstructure (all CGI) FOTV Vault-Tec Industries Building Ground Floor.png|Ground floor (dressed-up campus building) FOTV Vault-Tec Industries building.png|Composite image showing the entire building FOTV Vault-Tec Industries Building Suite 1.png|One of the suites in the building FOTV Vault-Tec Industries Building Suite 2.png FOTV Vault-Tec Industries Building Conference Room 1.png|The double-story conference room FOTV Vault-Tec Industries Building Conference Room 2.png FOTV Vault-Tec Industries Building Conference Room 3.png FOTV Vault-Tec Industries Building Conference Room 4.png FTV S2E6 Still 002.png FTV S2E6 Still 004.png FTV S2E6 Still 003.png ==References== {{References}} '''Meta''' [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]] [[Category:Vault-Tec Corporation]]

The '''headquarters of the United Nations''' is a mentioned-only location {{In|FO3}} and {{In|FOTV|noin}}.

==Background==
{{Main|United Nations}}
In May [[Timeline (2050-2099)#2052|2052]], as Earth's fossil fuel supplies began to dry up and nations began to [[Resource Wars|wage war with each other]] over the few resources that remained, the United Nations began to collapse under intense international squabbling, with many heated debates breaking out within their headquarters in [[New York City]].<ref group="Non-game">[[Fallout Bible 0#Timeline repair: Second strike|''Fallout Bible 0'']]: ''"2052 May-July: The United Nations, already suffering, begins to collapse. In a series of heated debates, many nations withdrew from the organization as the UN tried to keep the peace. At the end of July, the United Nations is disbanded."''</ref>

On July 26, 2052, at the height of global tensions over resource availability, the organization was formally disbanded. The sitting UN President at the time, [[Sakugama Okiri]], lamented the failure of global relations at a press conference held later in the building. The ambassadors of the few nations that remained in the headquarters were forced to vacate by the end of the week as a bidding war broke out over the building itself. As reported in the [[Washington, D.C.|D.C.]]-based ''[[Capital Post (company)|Capital Post]]'' newspaper, the toy company [[Bumbalo's]], in particular, hoped to turn the prime real estate into their new [[East Coast]] superstore.<ref>[[Capitol Post terminal entries#United Nations Disbanded.21|Capitol Post terminal entries; Capital Post Top Stories -- July 27, 2052, United Nations Disbanded!]]</ref>

Although the eventual buyer is unknown, training guides produced by the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] included a cartoon depiction of the UN building being overtaken with Vault-Tec logos. It remains unclear if this is a reflection of reality or merely a hyperbolic appropriation of the UN's imagery.<ref>"[[Step on the Gas!]]"</ref>

==Appearances==
The headquarters of the United Nations is mentioned only in ''Fallout 3''. A cartoon depiction appears in the ''[[Vault Seller's Survival Guide]]'' episode "[[Step on the Gas!]]"

([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) ==Layout== Situated on the southeast corner of the central section of the Strip, the building interior is divided into seven parts: ===Lobby and Casino=== The lobby and casino area contains the lobby and casino. The highly fashionable bar, "The Top Shelf," is also located in the entrance room that doubles as the casino. The drinks are overpriced, but that's the point. [[Mortimer (Fallout: New Vegas)|Mortimer]] can be found at the reception desk. The door to the cashier has an Average lock. There are three metal boxes within the cashier area at the bottom of a shelf that holds weapons and those of companions, and a variety of random [[Bottle cap (Fallout: New Vegas)|caps]] and small loot in the other safes and containers. ===The Gourmand=== {{Main|The Gourmand}} [[File:Ultra Luxe Gourmand.jpg|thumb|220px|The Gourmand]] The Gourmand is a famous restaurant run by temperamental chef and White Glove Society member [[Philippe]]. The restaurant is renowned for its famous [[brahmin Wellington]], and boasts a long waitlist, even though it usually seems sparsely populated. Gamblers, travelers and other Strip tourists found here will theorize the White Glove Society is more interested in maintaining the Gourmand's air of exclusivity than filling the restaurant, and are consequently padding the waitlist and arbitrarily denying access to customers. This suspicion is commented upon by [[Mr. New Vegas]] on [[Radio New Vegas]]. ===Kitchens=== The basement kitchens of the Ultra-Luxe are accessible from the members-only area, where the door is unlocked, and [[The Gourmand]], behind a door with an Easy lock. The basement itself consists of a number of rooms, including Philippe's actual kitchen, the pantry, the locked freezer containing [[Ted Gunderson]], an elevator back upstairs, and a wine room, containing a bottle of wine the player character can spike with sedatives as part of the quest [[Beyond the Beef]]. The basement hallways are regularly patrolled by a small group of three White Glove Society members, two of whom will initially be seen at the bottom of the first set of stairs "roasting" brahmin with flamers. They will confront the player character if they are caught in the basement without honorary White Glove Society membership or a White Glove Society disguise, and will turn hostile if the player cannot pass a [[Speech]] or [[Repair (Fallout: New Vegas)|Repair]] check. ===Members only area=== [[File:WG_Members_Only_area.jpg|thumb|220px]] The Ultra-Luxe members-only area consists of a large dining room, adjoining prep room, reception area, closet, and 10-12 members of the White Glove Society, some of which are armed with [[dress cane]]s and described as "[[White Glove bouncer|bouncers]]." The bouncers will be hostile towards the player character unless they have been inducted as an honorary member of the White Glove Society by [[Marjorie (Fallout: New Vegas)|Marjorie]], and subsequently been given a [[White Glove Society members key|key to the room]]. An alternative is to obtain a key and [[White Glove Society mask|White Glove mask]], and wear this disguise before entering the members-only area. An unlocked door in the prep area leads to the Ultra-Luxe's kitchens. ===Bathhouse=== [[File:UL bathhouse.jpg|thumb|220px|The bathhouse]] An indoor swimming pool converted into a bathhouse. It contains the steam room where the player character can meet the investigator's contact during the [[Beyond the Beef]] quest. Drinking the water from the bathhouse pool (HP 2, Rads 0) is considered theft, but harbors no Karma loss nor does it make anyone hostile. It is also stated that the salt in the bath is imported from California.[[Gambler (Fallout: New Vegas)|Gambler]]: ''"I heard they brought in sea salts from California just for this bath."''
([[VStreetNCRGambler.txt|Generic gambler's dialogue]]) {{clear}} ===Hotel rooms=== ====Bon Vivant suite==== [[File:Bon Vivant suite.jpg|thumb|220px]] {{main|Bon Vivant suite}} Access to the [[Bon Vivant suite]] is given to the player character for winning 11,250 [[Ultra-Luxe chip|chips]] in the casino. It is located in the hotel room area and is not to be mistaken for the penthouse suite in which Gunderson is staying. The room is average for the Ultra-Luxe and includes two beds that the Courier may sleep in. Most of the room's contents (containers, items, etc.) are set as "owned" and register as stealing if opened or taken. ===Penthouse suite=== [[File:Henderson_penthouse.jpg|thumb|220px|Henderson's penthouse]] [[Heck Gunderson]] is staying in this room, and has left several of his [[Gunderson hired hand|bodyguards]] here to watch the place. They will be hostile to the player character, so killing them or sneaking past them is required to loot the suite. The Courier needs a [[Ultra-Luxe penthouse key|key]], held only by the receptionist [[Mortimer (Fallout: New Vegas)|Mortimer]], to access the elevator to the suite. Mortimer can be killed or pickpocketed for the key. Alternatively, he can give the key to the player character during [[Beyond the Beef]] in some paths through that quest. In the situation one does not possess a key, a Lockpick skill of 75 allows access. Once inside the player character can see a small foyer leading to what appears to be a small guest dedicated portion of the luxury suite. Further inside the suite is quite grand and the ceiling is possibly the highest of all penthouse/presidential suites in New Vegas. In the middle of the large suite is a shallow pool and to the right is the dining room and kitchen. Upstairs is the master bedroom with a bar and the bathroom, including a pristine bathtub. Sleeping in the penthouse suite is impossible because the player character does not own the beds. ==Gambling== ; Games * The Ultra-Luxe offers [[Blackjack]] and [[Roulette]]. * The Ultra-Luxe pays 3:2 on blackjack, and the dealer must stand on all 17s. ; Rewards and ban Should the player acquire enough chips, the floor manager will offer increasingly valuable gifts, culminating in access to the [[Bon Vivant suite]]. * 3,750+ chips = [[Atomic cocktail]] * 7,500+ chips = [[Brahmin Wellington]] * 11,250+ chips = [[Bon Vivant suite key]] After the player character earns 15,000+ chips, they are banned from playing games at the Ultra-Luxe. Vault 24:
{{Infobox location |games =FOTV |mentions = |type = |owners =[[Vault-Tec Corporation]] (formerly) |image =FTV S2E1 Still 151.png }} '''Vault 24''' is a [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]] [[Vault]] located in the [[Mojave Wasteland]]. It appears as a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{in|FOTV}}, while a jumpsuit from the Vault was [[Fallout: New Vegas cut content|cut]] from {{In|FNV|noin}}. ==Background== {{Quotation|Individual is secondary to the collective. (Mandarin) ...true comrade chooses cooperation over individualism. (Mandarin) Our enemy has chosen the interest of product over the interest of people. We choose people over product. Freedom is inevitable. (Mandarin) The revolution will not be futile. (Mandarin)|Fragment of a mixed English/Chinese holotape used to recondition Vault dwellers. The tape alternates between the two languages and loops.}} [[file:FTV S2E1 Still 180.png|right|220px|thumb|The Ghoul picks up an ushanka with a red star, the international symbol of communism.]] Vault 24 was [[Vault#True purpose|designed]] to preserve and continue research into mind-control technologies, with [[Vault-Tec]]'s experimental staff using Americans assigned to the Vault as test subjects once the protocol was initiated. While they experimented with a variety of surgical techniques and reconditioning, the most successful was the [[brain-computer interface chip]] or "black box":[[Hank MacLean]]: "''Looks like a couple of the Vault experiments ran into some speed bumps. 24 made progress on the brain-computer interface.''" American dwellers fitted with this device were successfully converted to [[communism]], replacing Vault-Tec and American iconography with the flags of China, communist propaganda, and eschewing [[Vault jumpsuit]]s in favor of simple two-piece red garments with a prominent red star on the left-hand side and an ushanka with another red star bordered in gold.{{FOTV|2|1}} The Vault eventually failed, although the reasons for the failure are unclear. By 2296, mummified corpses of Vault dwellers litter the halls, some found still gathered at tables during what might be a council or soviet meeting, others still strapped to gurneys and medical chairs in the research laboratories, once forcibly made to watch videos meant to recondition them, with electrodes implanted into their brains. Once his true nature was revealed by [[Lee Moldaver]], the escaped [[Hank MacLean]] made his way to Vault 24 to seize the Vault's treasure trove of research. Vault laboratory 7HSZMS380200313 and the Vault itself was abandoned by this time, and he successfully took the data drive with him. [[Lucy MacLean]] and the [[Ghoul]] subsequently tracked him to the Vault, finding evidence of the Vault experiment within, and an [[Sunburned man|unfortunate victim]] of Hank's, who was used as a test subject to verify the functionality of the black box and leave a message for his daughter in gruesome fashion. ==Layout== [[File:FTV S2E1 Still 176.png|right|240px|thumb|The overgrown entrance hall]] Vault 24 was hidden beneath a [[Starlight Drive-in Theatre (TV series)|Starlight Drive-in Theatre]], with the Vault door concealed behind the movie screen. Inside the rocky outcropping was an arched entrance hall with a centrally-placed elevator granting access to the lower levels of the Vault. Damage to the structure of the Vault following its failure allowed sunlight and moisture to enter, leading to limited vegetation growing over the infrastructure, although nowhere near to the extent of places like [[Vault 22]]. The lower levels followed standard Vault-Tec designs, with living quarters provided for all dwellers. The experiment and provided supplies have led reconditioned dwellers to redecorate the Vault using modified [[Chinese]] flags to signify their newfound allegiance. The areas remained functional by 2297, although only low-power lighting was available by the time Hank MacLean entered the Vault. Below the living quarters lay the two-floor research level,The upper floor and stairs leading to it are visible when Lucy approaches the terminal. stocked with scientific and medical equipment necessary to continue work on the black box and perform the surgeries necessary for advancing the development of the brain-computer interface allowing for controlling minds. ==Notes== * Vault 24's experiment bears similarity to the story of [[Camp Liberty]] in ''Fallout 76'', introduced in the ''[[Skyline Valley (update)|Skyline Valley]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]]. Both Vault 24 and Camp Liberty used brainwashing techniques to turn their residents into adherents of communism, including through visual presentations that included hypnotic spiral imagery. Camp Liberty's experiment was part of [[Operation Sleeping Giant]], an initiative of the [[Defense Intelligence Agency]]. ==Appearances== Vault 24 appears in the ''Fallout'' TV series episode "[[The Innovator]]." ==Behind the scenes== {{FNVCC}} * A [[Vault jumpsuit (Fallout: New Vegas)#Vault 24 jumpsuit|Vault 24 jumpsuit]] was [[Fallout: New Vegas cut content|cut]] from ''Fallout: New Vegas''; it remains in the game files but can only be accessed with [[Fallout: New Vegas console commands|console commands]]. The Vault itself and any details regarding it cannot be found in the game. According to [[Joshua Sawyer]], the ''New Vegas'' developers did not make any concepts for Vault 24; the Vault itself was never intended to appear in-game, and its Vault jumpsuit may have been generated specifically for [[Sarah Weintraub]]'s unmarked quest [[Suits You, Sarah]].Question: '''I was reading up on New Vegas cut content and came across 'Vault 24', but apparently no plans or content beyond a jumpsuit exist for it in game files. Was there ever a concept planned for it? If not, what sort of concept would you have liked to explore?'''
[[Joshua Sawyer]]: ''I don’t believe so. I think we may have generated a few additional vault suits from vaults that we never intended to be in the game, but I can’t remember why. Maybe as part of a collection quest for Sarah Weintraub… ?''
([https://archive.is/Czn6Z Joshua Sawyer on Tumblr, 2019]) {{FNVCC|end}} [[File:FOTV Vault 24 Communist Flag.png|right|thumb|The Vault 24 communist flag.]] * The Vault in the TV series features communist iconography, including the [[propaganda flyer]] from ''[[Fallout 76]]'', which is visible in some background shots. Chinese flags include both the actual five star flag and a modified design pinned to the wall, where the stars are not gold, but a darker shade of red with a golden outline. * The phrase "The revolution will not be futile," heard in the communist brainwashing broadcasts in Vault 24, evokes "[[wikipedia:The Revolution Will Not Be Televised|The Revolution Will Not Be Televised]]," a spoken word song by [[wikipedia:Gil Scott-Heron|Gil Scott-Heron]] that focuses on the [[wikipedia:Black power movement|Black power movement]]. ==Gallery== ;TV series FTV S2E1 Still 151.png|Dogmeat discovers the entrance hidden behind the screen FTV S2E1 Still 152.png|Lucy takes notice of the Vault door FTV S2E1 Still 174.png|Inside the Vault FTV S2E1 Still 175.png|Overgrown entry hall FTV S2E1 Still 176.png|Detail shot of the interior FTV S2E1 Still 177.png|Ghoul inside the Vault FTV S2E1 Still 178.png|Vault door control pod FTV S2E1 Still 179.png|Elevator to the depths of the Vault FTV S2E1 Still 180.png|An ushanka with a gold-bordered red star, a communist emblem FTV S2E1 Still 181.png|Lucy standing by the control pod and the entry gantry FTV S2E1 Still 182.png|Lucy and the Ghoul board the elevator; entrance visual display units visible in the background FTV S2E1 Still 196.png|Lucy and the Ghoul arrive in the residential hallway of the Vault FTV S2E1 Still 197.png|Vault number painted on the wall FTV S2E1 Still 198.png|Meeting room with the [[Chinese]] flag on the wall and six dead Vault dwellers around the table. Wilds:
{{Infobox location |games =FOTV |type =landmark |image =FOTV The Wilds Panorama.png |part of =[[New California]] |factions =[[Brotherhood of Steel]] (2296) |creatures =[[Yao guai (TV series)|Yao guai]] }} The '''Wilds''' are a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== The region known as the "Wilds" is shown to be a vast stretch of [[New California]] which includes some pre-[[Great War|War]] cityscapes of [[Los Angeles]] that have been retaken by nature, distinguished by its dense woods punctuated by overgrown urban structures, home to populations of wildlife including hostile mutated types such as [[Gulper (TV series)|gulpers]] and [[Yao guai (TV series)|yao guai]]. ==In the TV series== In [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]], after escaping initial capture during his defection from the [[Enclave]] and subsequent flight from their [[Enclave research colony|mountainous research colony]], [[Siggi Wilzig]] and his canine companion [[CX404]] pass through the Wilds on a trek to reach the trading town of [[Filly]]. They eventually come to a clearing outside a cave where Wilzig tries to consume a trail ration of [[Cram]] but is interrupted by his dog returning with a severed human hand and subsequently run off by nearby danger.Events of {{FOTV|1|2}} Wilzig's escape was later discovered by the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 4)|Commonwealth Brotherhood of Steel]], who gave orders to a Brotherhood chapter called the [[Knights of San Fernando]], assigning them the mission of capturing Wilzig and his [[cold fusion|artifact]]. On the order of the San Fernando chapter's leader, [[Quintus|Elder Cleric Quintus]], several teams of [[Knight (TV series)|knights]] and their [[Brotherhood of Steel ranks#Squire|squires]] were sent to scour the Wilds in search of the Enclave defector.[[Quintus]]: "''Our mission comes from the highest clerics in the Commonwealth. It is believed that a denizen of the Enclave has escaped.''"
Squire: "''The Enclave's real?''"
Quintus: "''And that he has with him an object of profound potential to harm our nation or to save it. Each knight in this legion will search a section of the Wilds for this target. Brothers, we exist for moments such as these. Go forth with honor! And may the shape of the future be cut by your sword!''"
({{FOTV|1|1}}) One such team, composed of [[Titus|Knight Titus]] and his squire [[Maximus]] (replacing the original pick [[Dane (TV series)|Dane]]) disembarks from their vertibird in the section of the Wilds that Wilzig passed through. After coming across the scientist's campsite, the two investigate the cave suspecting that their target had been attacked and killed by its inhabitant. Subsequently, Titus is ambushed by the nesting yao guai, disarmed of his [[Heavy assault rifle (TV series)|heavy assault rifle]], and attempts to flee in terror but is chased down and lethally mauled by the creature. After killing the yao guai, before Maximus could administer life-saving first aid with a [[Stimpak (TV series)|stimpak]], Titus' threats and hostile behavior cause him to withhold and insult the knight in return, calling him a disgrace to the Brotherhood and the [[:File:Shady Sands Knight and Maximus.png|knight]] that Maximus idolizes. With his squire withholding medical care, Titus expires from his wounds, after which Maximus takes his armor and disguises himself as Titus to continue the mission on his own and prove his worth to the Brotherhood. ==Appearances== The Wilds appear only {{in|FOTV}} [[Fallout TV series episodes|episodes]] "The End" and "The Target." ==Behind the scenes== The establishing shot of the Wilds (used for the page) includes a foreground that is strikingly similar to [https://www.flickr.com/photos/cmdrcord/37481289074 Pripyat's Lenin Square], including the square itself, Palace of Culture Energetik, and the Polissya Pripyat hotel, though there is no supplementary evidence to date that it was used for a filming location. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Fallout TV series}} [[Category:New California]] [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]]

[[Cadillac Bob]] (writer; formerly) }} '''California Crest Studios''' was a pre-War [[Pre-War companies|motion picture company]] located in the [[Hollywood]] district of [[Los Angeles]], [[California]]. Its main studio lot appears as a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== California Crest Studios was founded before the [[Great War]] and operated primarily in the [[Hollywood]] district of Los Angeles. Its main studio is located not far from a section of the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame]].At the beginning of "[[The Ghouls]]", [[Lucy MacLean|Lucy]] and [[the Ghoul]] are shown walking along a section of the Hollywood Walk of Fame, then at the end of "[[The Head]]," they pass by the ruins of California Crest Studios, indicating the two locations are within walking distance of each other. The company was well-known as the makers of the highly successful Western movie ''[[The Man from Deadhorse]]'' starring [[Cooper Howard]], and had already begun working on a sequel to the film around January 2077.[[Fallout - A Special LIVE Report from Galaxy News]] news ticker: ''NO ONE'S BEATING THIS DEADHORSE. "THE MAN FROM DEADHORSE" TOPS BOX OFFICE. A SEQUEL IS ALREADY IN THE WORKS AT CALIFORNIA CREST STUDIOS.'' As of that month, they had also signed a deal with the [[Nuka-Cola Corporation]] for a seventeen-film series featuring the Nuka-Cola mascots [[Bottle]] and [[Cappy]].[[Fallout - A Special LIVE Report from Galaxy News]] news ticker: ''NUKA-COLA MASCOTS 'BOTTLE AND CAPPY' TO APPEAR IN ANIMATED FILM FROM CALIFORNIA CREST STUDIOS. WILL BE THE FIRST IN A SEVENTEEN PICTURE DEAL BETWEEN THE COMPANIES.'' The studio worked with film services businesses such as catering company [[Catering to the Stars!]] and transportation and equipmental rental firm [[Studio Services]], and also operated a bus tour service, California Crest Studio Tours, for tourists visiting its physical location. The company was also known to utilize [[Mister Handy (TV series)|Mister Handy]] robotic units in their operations. Like much of the greater Los Angeles area, the bombs dropping reduced the studio building to rubble, with the desert winds and rolling sands of the [[wasteland]] gradually swallowing it up over the years. ==In the TV series== ===[[The Head]]=== In the first of two flashbacks to Cooper's life in the pre-War era, he is filming the final scene of his movie ''The Man from Deadhorse'' at the studio but cuts near the end and expresses his discomfort to the film's director [[Emil Dale]] about how his sheriff character is scripted to shoot and kill the outlaw played by his co-star [[Jorge]] rather than arresting him alive as always happens in his Western films. When Emil fails to convince him of the creative choices behind the decision, Cooper wants to involve one of the writers [[Cadillac Bob]] but is informed about the man's firing due to supposedly holding [[Communism|communist]] beliefs. Cooper's conversation with Emil is cut short when he sees his wife [[Barb Howard|Barb]] nearby. The loving partners share a touching moment when she tricks him into eating lavender taffy which he hates, before Barb hands him a package containing a [[Vault jumpsuit]] to wear for his promotional shoot in collaboration with Barb's employer, the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]]. Cooper reluctantly agrees, then opts to race their daughter [[Janey Howard|Janey]] to his trailer. In the present of [[Timeline#2296|2296]], [[the Ghoul]] and a captive [[Lucy MacLean]] march onto the site of the ruined California Crest Studios lot during the trek from [[Hollywood Boulevard]] to a [[Super Duper Mart (TV series)|Super Duper Mart]] near [[Santa Monica Boulevard]]. The bounty hunter stops at one point to survey the ruins, remembering the times long ago when he worked there as an actor. Lucy tries to beg for some nourishing water, but the Ghoul cruelly dumps the rest of his canteen onto the ground and then mockingly suggests she try drinking from a nearby irradiated pond. As they near the lot of the old studios, Lucy sees a pre-War billboard with [[Vault Boy]] on it right before the Ghoul shoots a hole through the mascot's face in quiet anger and they carry on.Events of {{FOTV|1|3}} In the second flashback, Cooper emerges from his trailer on the CCS lot dressed up in his jumpsuit, which Barb reveals she personally designed to incorporate the signature blue-and-gold color scheme of his sheriff character. Cooper then walks with his family through the backlot to the site of the promo shoot. There, Barb introduces him to Vault-Tec reps [[George Yaffe]] and [[Sarah Clements]]. Though they initially share banter, the reps fall awkwardly silent after Cooper asks if the jumpsuits are really [[radiation]]-proof, then hastily answer positively. As the shoot is getting ready to start, Cooper makes an off-hand suggestion to add a thumbs-up gesture, an idea the Vault-Tec employees applaud. ==Layout== What is shown of the company's assets in the TV series indicates that California Crest Studios consisted of a large number of hangars used for filming, with roads in between where props, actors' trailers, and other services could be located for shooting. The studios also had a large, two-story blue house with a large bronze statue of a woman holding a wireframe globe outside it. By 2296 long after the nuclear apocalypse, there is almost no trace left of the area except for the ruins of the house and the destroyed statue, along with some other smaller ruined houses some distance away from the area. ==Appearances== California Crest Studios appears only {{In|FOTV}} [[Fallout TV series episodes|episode]] "[[The Head]]" and was first mentioned in ''[[Fallout - A Special LIVE Report from Galaxy News]]'', a promotional video for the TV series. ==Behind the scenes== The post-War ruins of the California Crest Studios lot were filmed at the casino of [[wikipedia:Elizabeth Bay|Elizabeth Bay, Namibia]], a ghost town and former diamond mine. Other areas of the town were used to film various other scenes, such as the [[Santa Monica|Santa Monica Pier]] and abandoned houses shown in "[[The Target]]." ==Gallery== California Crest Studios.png|California Crest Studios backlot FOTV Roman actors.png|Romans FOTV California Crest Studios bus.png|Tour bus FOTV California Crest Studios ruins 1.png|Ruins FOTV California Crest Studios ruins 2.png|Ruins FOTV California Crest Studios ruins 3.png|Ruins FOTV California Crest Studios ruins 4.png|The Ghoul stares at the ruins ==References== {{References}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group=Meta}} {{Navbox pre-War companies}} [[Category:California Crest Studios]] [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]]

 }} {{Quotation|Silver Rush: Feel the rush of a warm laser in your hand.{{Inline quote|sound=FNV MrNewVegas FeelTheRush.ogg}}|[[Mr. New Vegas]]|''[[Fallout: New Vegas]]''}} The '''Silver Rush''' is an [[Fallout: New Vegas locations#Freeside|unmarked location]] within [[Freeside]] in the [[Mojave Wasteland]] {{In|FNV}}. It also appears in [[Fallout TV series season 2|season 2]] of {{in|FOTV|noin}}. ==Background== {{Quotation|The Silver Rush casino was in competition with The Atomic Wrangler until the owners ran afoul of the Van Graff family.|[[Fallout: New Vegas loading screens|''Fallout: New Vegas'' loading screens]]}} Established in [[Timeline#2071|2071]],[[:File:FNV-CE-PlayingCard-SilverRush.png|Silver Rush playing card]] the Silver Rush Casino rivaled the [[Atomic Wrangler Casino]] on their shared space along [[Fremont Street]] in [[New Vegas|Las Vegas]], [[Nevada]]. Following the [[Great War]], new owners reestablished the old casino sometime prior to [[Timeline#2281|2281]], even reigniting the old rivalry with the Atomic Wrangler. That lasted until the arrival of the [[Van Graffs]] in the Mojave seeking to expand their arms-trading business. Setting their sights on the Silver Rush, the Van Graffs swept in and "evicted" the former owners, throwing out all the casino hardware to make room for their stockpile of [[Energy Weapons (Fallout: New Vegas)|energy weapons]].[[Fallout: New Vegas loading screens|''Fallout: New Vegas'' loading screens]]: ''"The Silver Rush casino was in competition with The Atomic Wrangler until the owners ran afoul of the Van Graff family."'' When the [[Kings]] showed up to protest the change in management, the Van Graffs gave them a first-hand taste of their weaponry, reducing some of their number to goo, after which the two groups have left each other alone ever since.The [[Courier]]: ''"Tell me about the Kings."''
[[Gloria Van Graff]]: ''"Ah, the "rulers" of Freeside. The Kings are a bunch of boys who refuse to grow up, and this is their playground. Their leader seems different, though. The few times I've dealt with him I've been impressed despite myself. Unfortunately, he rarely acts. The Kings believe that everyone in Freeside can do whatever they want, provided they can back it up with force. Which suits us just fine. When we first arrived in Freeside, the Kings protested when we kicked out the original occupant of this establishment. When we reduced several of their members to glowing puddles of goo, their objections vanished. Since then, we've left each other alone."''
([[Gloria Van Graff's dialogue]]) Initially, the Silver Rush weapons depot was headed by [[Frieda Van Graff]], but she soon left to pursue personal interests.[[Courier]]: ''"Tell me about your siblings."''
[[Jean-Baptiste Cutting]]: ''"We're a wild bunch. There's my sister Frieda, who used to run this branch but took off to pursue "the opportunity of a lifetime", as she put it."''
([[VFSJeanBaptisteCutting.txt#49|Jean-Baptiste Cutting's dialogue]]) After Frieda's departure, her sister [[Gloria Van Graff]] and brother [[Jean-Baptiste Cutting]] were assigned to head the Silver Rush. They soon capitalized on the Silver Rush's proximity to the Atomic Wrangler by forgoing any sort of rivalry and instead making it attractive to the casino's customers with pockets full of [[Bottle cap (Fallout: New Vegas)|caps]] from [[gambling]].The [[Courier]]: ''"What is there to do here?"''
[[Gloria Van Graff]]: ''"Well, you probably noticed the Atomic Wrangler across the street. That's pretty much the place to go around here. They make it a little loud around here at night, but the business their proximity brings more than makes up for it. Other than them, you're better off skipping Freeside entirely and just heading to the Strip."''
([[VFSGloriaVanGraff.txt|Gloria Van Graff's dialogue]]) Under the control of the affluent Van Graffs, the Silver Rush is not lacking in security and any kind of theft is dealt with swiftly. Since Freeside and energy weapons seem an unlikely duo, the idea of starting a business trading them in the area would seem doomed to fail, however, Gloria boasts that because the Van Graffs do not sell cheap merchandise, their customers do not care where they have to go to purchase from them.The [[Courier]]: ''"This seems like a bad neighborhood to open a store."''
[[Gloria Van Graff]]: ''"First, we don't lack for security. I'm not worried about anyone breaking in here or stealing our goods. Not that we don't occasionally have attempts, but even those prove useful. Do you know how much target dummies cost? Back to my point, the second thing you'll notice is that we do not sell cheap merchandise. Everything here is second-to-none. People who buy Van Graff goods typically don't care where they have to go to get them."''
([[VFSGloriaVanGraff.txt|Gloria Van Graff's dialogue]]) ==Layout== Situated in the northwestern corner of the southern section of Freeside, the building is identifiable by its lopsided sign situated on the top of the partially collapsed roof, past the Atomic Wrangler's own neon fixture. The main room of the interior is outfitted with a counter, displaying of energy weapons and ammunition. A shelf close to the door has a large amount of ammunition, [[Plasma grenade (Fallout: New Vegas)|plasma grenades]], and mines. Down a short hallway in the back of the accessible part of the store is a bathroom. The cashier's room is barricaded and locked. Past the locked door there are some [[Safe (Fallout: New Vegas)|safe]]s, a locked [[terminal]], and a stairway to the living quarters. Five [[Van Graff thug]]s are stationed inside, two flanking the front door, two around the cashier room, and one walking back and forth between the two. The upper floor of the building (directly behind the sign) can be accessed from the second floor of the neighboring ruined building directly to the northwest. The [[Courier]] may hop up the debris piles to reach a bedroom, complete with mattress and a small dining table that overlooks the street below. ==Notable loot== * [[Letter to Gloria]] - Inside the Hard-locked safe in the backroom, just before the stairs. Relevant as a [[quest item]] for a certain part of [[Heartache by the Number]]. * [[Van Graff key]] - Carried by Gloria, Jean-Baptiste, and every Van Graff thug in and outside the building including [[Simon (Fallout: New Vegas)|Simon]]. * [[Cleansing Flame (GRA)|Cleansing Flame]] {{Icon|FNVGRA}} - Sold by Gloria. * [[Sprtel-Wood 9700 (GRA)|Sprtel-Wood 9700]] {{Icon|FNVGRA}} - Sold by Gloria. * [[The Smitty Special (GRA)|The Smitty Special]] {{Icon|FNVGRA}} - Sold by Gloria. ==Related quests== * [[Birds of a Feather]] * [[Heartache by the Number]] * [[Tend to Your Business]] ==Notes== * All weapons and ammunition in the store can be stolen without [[Karma (Fallout: New Vegas)|Karma]] loss, but the guards will turn hostile if the player character is caught, making it impossible to start Birds of a Feather, or leading the quest to fail if it was already started. * Before entering the Silver Rush, [[Simon (Fallout: New Vegas)|Simon]] (named "Van Graff thug" prior to starting Birds of a Feather) will take all the player character's weapons, including [[holdout weapons]], and store them in the dark metal crate next to the entrance. The weapons will be returned when leaving the Silver Rush. After starting Birds of a Feather, the guards will stop taking weapons on entry. * Upon entering the Silver Rush for the first time, a scripted event occurs between Gloria Van Graff and [[Soren|a customer]] who owes them money. Four [[Van Graff thug]]s block the walkways to the inner room behind the fence. Any attempt to move past the guards prior to the completion of the scripted event will result in all Silver Rush inhabitants becoming hostile. * If [[Arcade Gannon]] is present as a companion when entering the Silver Rush for the first time, his scripted response related to [[For Auld Lang Syne]] may interrupt and/or delay the completion of the Silver Rush scripted event with Gloria. The player character must wait behind the fence near the entrance to allow the scripted event to complete and avoid hostility with the inhabitants. * All occupants in the Silver Rush will be hostile towards the player character either upon killing Gloria or reporting them to the NCR during Heartache by the Number, forcing hostility one way or another. Afterward, the entire store's inventory can be taken without penalty. * During Birds of a Feather, if the fourth "customer" is allowed inside while standing outside the doors with [[Simon (Fallout: New Vegas)|Simon]] and the building is blown up, killing the Van Graffs, the player character can still hand the "agreement" evidence to [[Jackson (Mojave Outpost)|Ranger Jackson]] at the [[Mojave Outpost]] to complete the peaceful ending of Heartache by the Number if it was retrieved beforehand. This method does not fail the quest, and no one will treat it as if all the occupants were killed. If visiting with Cass, she will be mad about the decision to kill the Van Graffs, but if returning to Jackson, it will not affect the result. ==Appearances== The Silver Rush appears {{In|FNV}} and {{in|FOTV|noin}}. ==Behind the scenes== * The in-game Silver Rush is located in the same geographical area as the real-world [[wikipedia:Golden Nugget Las Vegas|Golden Nugget Hotel and Casino]] located in the [[wikipedia:Fremont Street Experience|Fremont Street Experience]] of Las Vegas, Nevada. The former sign, now located at the [[wikipedia:Neon Museum|Neon Museum]], resembles the in-game equivalent. * The name Silver Rush is a reference to [[wikipedia:Silver mining in Nevada|the real-world silver mining history]] of Nevada, especially in the years following the discovery of the "[[wikipedia:Comstock Lode|Comstock Lode]]" in 1858, close to Virginia City, Nevada. ==Bugs== *{{Platforms|pc,ps3,xbox360}} When entering the Silver Rush the first time, the scripted event might randomly freeze at various points.{{Verify|verified}} ** Sometimes reloading the autosave from entering will resolve the problem. Using the console commands "kill" and "resurrect" in sequence on Jean-Baptiste can also fix the issue. Leaving and re-entering, then talk to her to receive Birds of a Feather can also fix it. Using the console command ''set "10d8e5".ShootingVolunteer to 1'', which advances the script past the part where it sticks also works. Another possible fix is to open the console and type "prid 0010d8e7", then type "say VFSVanGraffLaughter". * {{Platforms|pc,ps3,xbox360}} If weapons are stolen from the table, then the auto-save gained from entering the Silver Rush is loaded the previously stolen weapons will be in full condition after the save loads.{{Verify|verified}} *{{Platforms|pc,ps3,xbox360}} Sometimes stolen energy weapons will stack in the inventory but will be displayed as a single item. Dropping an item of that type fixes this.{{Verify|verified}} *{{Platforms|pc,ps3,xbox360}} Sometimes, the inventory of Gloria never updates according to character level, selling only the same low-level weapons.{{Verify|verified}} **This glitch can be fixed by saving right in front of Gloria, quitting the game to the main menu, and reloading that save. This should restock Gloria's inventory. *{{Platforms|xbox360}} With the [[Mysterious Stranger (Fallout: New Vegas)|Mysterious Stranger]] perk, and after completing Heartache by the Number without killing the Van Graffs, if the Courier quickly targets a thug and kills him in V.A.T.S mode, the [[Mysterious Stranger (character)|Mysterious Stranger]] will be completely invisible and can be targeted with V.A.T.S mode. He will be there forever afterward and if damaged enough will become hostile.{{Verify|verified}} *{{Platforms|pc,ps3,xbox360}} Sometimes, when entering the Silver Rush with a companion, it is possible that the companion will disappear, while still showing on the map, but invisible and completely static.{{Verify|verified}} *{{Platforms|pc}} Entering the Silver Rush for the time may spawn doubles of Jean-Baptiste, Gloria, and the captive Van Graff guard, who will be standing between the bound guard and Jean-Baptiste. The scripted event will still happen with no issue, though Jean-Baptiste's laser will hit the unbound guard and reduce him to ash. KPSS radio station:
{{Infobox location |games =FOTV |image =FOTV KPSS station.png |part of =[[Los Angeles]] * [[Hollywood Hills]] |factions = |owners =[[DJ Carl]] }} The '''KPSS radio station''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== The radio station was constructed at the base of [[Hollywood Hills]] near the city of [[Los Angeles]], on a forested hill surrounded by desert. By the late [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2290s]], the sole occupant of KPSS is the radio host [[Carl (TV series)|Carl]], who fills the airtime entirely with a large collection of vintage fiddle music. Carl does not take visitors at the station, with an array of defensive traps, including massive bear traps and makeshift crossbows linked to tripwires, surrounding the main building to ensure anyone looking to place a request or make a complaint about his choice of music would sooner have an arrow lodged in their vital parts.[[Carl (TV series)|DJ Carl]] (via radio): ''"Hey-yo, this Is DJ Carl at KPSS, broadcasting from the base of the once-beautiful Hollywood Hills. Like most weeks here at KPSS, this week is fiddle week, when all of my airtime will be spent luxuriating in my small but mighty collection of fiddle tunes. So, I'd encourage you to sit back and enjoy the folksy, gutsy sound of bygone fiddlers. And, if you don't like what you hear, just a reminder that I don't take visitors to the station. A simple postcard will suffice. That said, enjoy the fiddling."''
{{FOTV|1|7}} The station exterior is littered with the displayed heads of those Carl refers to as his "[[critic]]s."[[Thaddeus]]: ''"Great job on these booby traps, by the way. Really good."''
[[Carl (TV series)|DJ Carl]]: ''"Hey, thanks."''
Thaddeus: ''"Yeah. That one's crazy."''
DJ Carl: ''"Critics."''
Thaddeus: ''"Yeah. People just, uh, can’t be nice."''
({{FOTV|1|7}}) ==In the TV series== ===[[The Radio]]=== After abandoning [[CX404]] at the [[Red Rocket (TV series)|Red Rocket]] gas station, [[Thaddeus]] eventually arrives at the radio station carrying [[Siggi Wilzig]]'s head and requests the usage of Carl's broadcasting equipment to get a message to the [[Brotherhood of Steel]] for retrieval, meanwhile complimenting his choice of music and booby trap setup.{{FOTV|1|7}} Sometime later, he spots [[Lucy MacLean]] and [[Maximus]] approaching and, still viewing the latter as a traitor to the Brotherhood, attempts to shoot at them with his [[10mm pistol (TV series)|10mm pistol]] but misses every shot. While stumbling back, Thaddeus ends up triggering one of Carl's traps and gets a crossbow bolt shot through his neck. He only survives the wound due to the [[snake oil salesman]]'s [[elixir]] that he consumed. Thaddeus realizes however that once the Brotherhood learns of his mutation, they will execute him immediately, to which Lucy is confused about why the "good guys" would do that only for both Brotherhood members to agree that it's "complicated."[[Maximus]]: ''"The Brotherhood."''
[[Thaddeus]]: ''"Oh, fuck. Shit. Oh, fuck! Oh, fuck. They'll kill me if they find out."''
[[Lucy MacLean]]: ''"What? This-this is good, no? The Brotherhood is the good guys?"''
Thaddeus: ''"Uh, it's a complicated organization."''
({{FOTV|1|7}}) Maximus then asks Thaddeus to hand over the head and artifact and tells him to flee, which Thaddeus does after first thanking his former comrade. Maximus then gives Wilzig's head to Lucy and takes one of the critic heads, disfiguring it to make it unrecognizable to the Brotherhood so that he could buy Lucy time to bring the real head to [[Lee Moldaver|Moldaver]] and save her [[Hank MacLean|father]]. Before leaving, Lucy gives him a kiss and a promise that she will wait for him to meet her at [[Vault 33]]. Maximus smiles before turning to face the approaching squad of [[Vertibird (TV series)|vertibirds]]. ==Notes== The instrumental fiddle music playing during the scenes at KPSS was originally composed by [[Heather MacArthur]] and previously appeared in ''[[Fallout 4]]'' as a track played on [[Radio Freedom]], the radio station associated with the [[Commonwealth Minutemen]]. To that end, Prime Video X-Ray and the series' [[Fallout TV series soundtrack|official soundtrack]] identify the version used in the show as "Minutemen Radio."As seen on the [[Fallout TV series soundtrack#Licensed songs|''Fallout'' TV series soundtrack]] ==Appearances== The KPSS radio station appears only {{in|FOTV}} [[Fallout TV series episodes|episode]] "[[The Radio]]." ==Gallery== FOTV KPSS More Distant Shot.png|Lucy and Maximus approach FOTV KPSS Distant Shot.png FOTV KPSS Logo.png FOTV KPSS Closeup with Thaddy.png FOTV KPSS Overhead Shot.png ==References== {{References}} [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]] [[ru:Радиостанция «КПСС»]]

He's a sight. You probably already saw him when you came in, but you can go up inside, too.|[[Jeannie May Crawford]]|sound=FNV JeannieMayCrawford DinkyTheTownMascot.ogg}} '''Dinky the T-Rex''' is an [[Fallout: New Vegas locations#Independent towns|unmarked location]] within [[Novac]] in the [[Mojave Wasteland]] {{In|FNV}}. It also appears in [[Fallout TV series season 2|season 2]] of {{in|FOTV|noin}}, as well as ''[[Fallout Shelter]]''. ==Background== Dinky has served as a roadside attraction in the area around Novac since before the [[Great War]], additionally serving as a revenue source with the [[Dino Bite gift shop]] situated inside of it. By [[Timeline#2281|2281]], the tourist attraction now doubly serves as a sniper's nest, specifically the balcony housed in its jaws, utilized by Novac's resident pair of retired [[First Recon]] sharpshooters, [[Manny Vargas]] and [[Craig Boone]]; both take shifts defending the town during the day and night, respectively.''[[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition Tour of the Mojave Wasteland|Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition]]'' p. 410, Dinky the Dinosaur's Mouth: ''"Depending on the time of day, you’ll encounter Manny Vargas (days) or Boone (nights) at this location.''"''[[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition Tour of the Mojave Wasteland|Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition]]'' p. 410, Manny Vargas' room: ''"The sniper in the mouth of Dinky the Dinosaur that watches over Novac during the day is Manny Vargas.''"''[[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition Tour of the Mojave Wasteland|Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition]]'' p. 410, Craig Boone's room: ''"The sniper in the mouth of Dinky that watches Novac at nighttime is Boone. This is his room, and if he’s in it, he tells you to get out, and meet him up in the mouth at 9 PM.''" ==Layout== Situated within the [[Dino Dee-lite Motel]] complex,[[Rose of Sharon Cassidy|Cass]]: ''"Named this place after the hotel. NoVac's the hotel, not the lizard.''"
([[RoseofSharonCassidy.txt|Cass' dialogue]]) Dinky is situated along [[Highway 95]], visible from a distance due to its height.[[Rose of Sharon Cassidy|Cass]]: ''"Can see Dinky for miles, good landmark.''"
([[RoseofSharonCassidy.txt|Cass' dialogue]])''[[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition Tour of the Mojave Wasteland|Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition]]'' p. 25: ''"Novac [5.18] is worth visiting for more than just Dinky the dinosaur; you can stay at the motel, and use the Workbench in town, as well as trading with vendors that wander down Highway 95 to reach here.''" The [[T-Rex]] holds the thermometer, having taken a bite out of the top, that advertises the motel and amenities such as color television.[[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide faction profiles#Novac|''Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide'' faction profiles]], p. 43: ''"Watching over them is the landmark of the area: a giant fabricated tyrannosaurus rex biting off the top of "The World's 2nd Largest Thermometer". The interior of "Dinky" also serves as the city center (a converted gift shop from pre-war times, with a sniper's nest in Dinky's mouth). Dinky is the "attraction" that drew in tourists.''" The structure can be accessed from the left or right of the Novac fence. A door and set of stairs on the side of the dinosaur is the entrance to [[Dino Bite gift shop]]. Another interior set of stairs provides access to the mouth. There is a room behind the counter containing rocket souvenirs.''[[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition Tour of the Mojave Wasteland|Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition]]'' p. 412, Dinky the Dinosaur: Dino Bite gift shop: ''"Up the steps, and into the stomach of Dinky, there’s a gift shop run by Cliff Briscoe.''" The motel itself is located behind Dinky, across the courtyard. ==Notable loot== * [[That Gun]] - Sold by [[Cliff Briscoe]] in the gift shop. Can also be stolen (incurring [[Karma (Fallout: New Vegas)|Karma]] loss) by entering the closet full of rocket souvenirs and taking it from a shelf. * [[1st Recon beret]] - Given by Boone in the sniper's nest after completing [[One for My Baby]] by finding the correct culprit. * {{Icon|FNVGRA}} [[Paciencia (GRA)|Paciencia]] - Sold by Cliff Briscoe in the gift shop. * {{Icon|FNVGRA}} [[MF Hyperbreeder Alpha (GRA)|MF Hyperbreeder Alpha]] - Sold by Cliff Briscoe in the gift shop. ==Notes== * If [[Rose of Sharon Cassidy|Cass]] is brought to Novac, she states that she initially thought Dinky was a giant [[Gecko (Fallout: New Vegas)|gecko]].[[Rose of Sharon Cassidy|Cass]]: ''"First saw this place, thought the giant gecko was real. Read a book that giant lizards walked the earth like this one - might be a gecko this size.''"
([[RoseofSharonCassidy.txt|Cass' dialogue]]) * One of [[Follows-Chalk]]'s idle comments references Dinky, as he questions the [[Courier]] if there "really [is] a giant thunder-lizard people live inside."[[Follows-Chalk]]: ''"I hear some odd things about the civilized lands outside Zion. Is there really a giant thunder-lizard people live inside?"''
([[NVDLC02FollowsChalk.txt|Follows-Chalk's dialogue]]) * In ''Fallout: New Vegas'', Dinky is facing towards the roadway. However, in the TV series, he was rotated 180 degrees and is now facing towards the motel. * A buildable [[CAMP|C.A.M.P.]] and [[Fallout 76 workshop objects|workshop object]] version of Dinky the T-Rex, known as the [[Dino Bite gift shop (Fallout 76)|Dino Bite gift shop]], was made available to [[Fallout 1st]] members through the [[Atomic Shop]] in ''[[Fallout 76]]'', beginning in December 2025. A Dinky [[plushie]] was also made available at the same time. ==Appearances== Dinky the T-Rex appears {{In|FNV}}, {{in|FOTV|noin}}, and {{in|FOS|noin}}. It is also mentioned {{in|FO76}}, as well as indirectly in the ''Fallout: New Vegas'' [[Fallout: New Vegas add-ons|add-on]] ''[[Honest Hearts]]''. ==Behind the scenes== * The landmark closely resembles Mr. Rex, one of two large biomorphic buildings designed and constructed by sculptor [[wikipedia:Cabazon Dinosaurs|Claude K.
