"[[City of Lost Angels]]"{{Inline quote|sound=City of Lost Angels.ogg}}
 {{Quotation|Often the first place NCR travelers stop after the Mojave Outpost, Primm is also where a lot of folks realize they left New Vegas with barely enough money to make the long trek back to The Hub.|[[Fallout: New Vegas loading screens|''Fallout: New Vegas'' loading screens]]}} '''Primm''' is a [[Fallout: New Vegas locations#Independent towns|location]] in the [[Mojave Wasteland]] {{In|FNV}}. It also appears in the background and in a credits sequence in [[Fallout TV series season 2|season 2]] of {{in|FOTV|noin}}. Often touted as the "poor man's [[New Vegas|Vegas]]," both before and after the bombs, in the 23rd century the town saw a surge of financial success from its location along [[Interstate 15]] and proximity to the [[Mojave Outpost]] managing the caravan traffic to and from the [[New California|Core Regions]] of the [[New California Republic]]. Around late [[Timeline#2281|2281]], however, the fallout of the [[NCRCF prison break|breakout]] at the nearby [[NCR Correctional Facility]] reached Primm's limits as violent [[escaped convict]]s besieged the town, killing the [[McBain (male)|sheriff]], driving most residents out, capturing [[Beagle|some others]], and forcing the rest to seek refuge in the [[Vikki and Vance Casino]], hoping for NCR support or a miracle out of the desert. ==Background== ===Pre-War=== Before the [[Great War]], Primm was a small resort town located in Clark County, Nevada, sitting alongside [[Interstate 15]] connecting [[Boneyard|Los Angeles]] and [[New Vegas|Las Vegas]]. Quickly garnering a reputation as a "poor man's Las Vegas," Primm allowed tourists from [[State#California|California]] to get a taste of "Sin City" on the way in or lose what remained of their savings on the way out. The resort had a number of tourist attractions to boost its appeal, including the [[Vikki and Vance Casino]], dedicated to a pair of outlaws who were the southwest answer to [[Wikipedia:Bonnie and Clyde|Bonnie and Clyde]], and the [[Bison Steve Hotel|Bison Steve Casino and Hotel]] boasting the Mojave region's largest and most rickety rollercoaster, [[El Diablo rollercoaster|El Diablo]].''[[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide]] Collector's Edition'' p.44: ''"'''Primm'''"''
''"Pre-war, Primm was 'budget Vegas', a tiny town where Californians could go to gamble, the shortest distance between their wallets and a hole in the ground. Now it's not much of a settlement at all, poorly populated to begin with and more treacherous since the Powder Gangs broke out of prison. The landscape of Primm is dominated by a few empty ranch homes, the rubble of the town's main streets and store-fronts, and a small NCR camp set up southwest of town to prevent Convicts from pushing further south to the NCR's Mojave Outpost. The townsfolk, now without a sheriff after he was murdered by Gangers, are hold up across the road from the Mojave Express Couriers, in the down-trodden old Vikki & Vance Casino. Low on supplies, the townsfolk can't hold out much longer, and the Convicts' presence continues to build as they've recently commandeered the larger Bison Steve Casino and Hotel, patrolling the unstable El Diablo rollercoaster and wrecking the remaining grandeur this place once had. Primm faces a grim reality; there are few people here to keep order."''
([[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide faction profiles]])''[[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide]] Collector's Edition'' pp. 385-388: ''"'''[4.17] Primm'''''
''Pre-War, Primm was 'budget Vegas', a tiny town where Californians could go to gamble, the shortest distance between their wallets and a hole in the ground. Now it's not much of a settlement at all, poorly populated to begin with and more treacherous since the Powder Gangs broke out of prison. Wastelanders have scouted out Primm for a settlement in recent years, but even at its "prime," it was unlikely to have had a large population. To attempt to woo potential travelers along the then-freeway, two "themed" casinos where built around the exploits of two desperadoes from ancient history, and an archaic (and now highly dangerous) rollercoaster."''
([[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition Tour of the Mojave Wasteland]])The [[Courier]]: ''"Tell me about Primm."''
[[Primm Slim]]: ''"Primm is a thriving resort community located in Clark County, Nevada, right along Interstate 15. Whether you can't wait 'til Vegas to try your luck, or want to hit one last jackpot before you leave Nevada, Primm's your place! The town's Primm-eer attraction is the world-famous Vikki and Vance Casino and Museum, so you came to the right place, pardner!"''
([[PrimmSlim.txt|Primm Slim's dialogue]]) ===Post-War=== The town lost much of its appeal after the nuclear apocalypse, as survivors and later wastelanders had other concerns besides gambling their meager earnings away. Primm however remained, even developing a small, tightly knit community over time. In the late 23rd century, as the [[New California Republic]] expanded into the Mojave from [[New California]], Primm's proximity to the [[Mojave Outpost]] resulted in it becoming a promising trade town, benefiting from the growing traffic to and from [[New Vegas]], both civilian and military. For all who couldn't or wouldn't want to reach New Vegas, its "Las Vegas on a budget" appeal was revived with the town offering a casino, hotel, several shops and a courier waystation. Unlike its neighbor to the southeast, [[Nipton]], its reputation as a small spot of safety and respite was maintained through having active law enforcement via the town sheriff.The [[Courier]]: ''"Primm has seen better days."''
[[Knight (Mojave Outpost)|Knight]]: ''"{{Tooltip|It has. It was a promising trade town - before the escape at the correctional facility.|{Sad} }} {{Tooltip|Lost a good bit of money at the Vikki and Vance.|{Shakes head, recalling a bad memory} }}"''
([[VMOMajorKnight.txt|Knight's dialogue]])The [[Courier]]: ''"{{Tooltip|His sentence was almost up, and he isn't tied to the Powder Gangers.|}}"''
[[Knight (Mojave Outpost)|Knight]]: ''"[SUCCEEDED] Hmm.{{Tooltip| |{Pensive pause} }}All right. If his sentence was closing up I can see about getting him pardoned. Primm is important to our trade up from California, so having someone there who owes us a favor... that couldn't hurt."''
([[VMOMajorKnight.txt|Knight's dialogue]]) However, Primm's good fortune turned for the worse again in [[Timeline#2281|2281]] with the [[NCRCF prison break|breakout]] at the [[NCR Correctional Facility]] to the northeast. Soon after, [[escaped convict]]s started wreaking havoc along I-15, gradually encroaching on Primm itself. Around a month before the [[Courier]] was ambushed outside [[Goodsprings]], a group of convicts, distinct from the more organized [[Powder Gangers]], stormed the town, killing the sheriff and his wife in their sleep as well as taking the lone deputy [[Beagle]] hostage in the Bison Steve, and effectively put a stranglehold on Primm's economy.The [[Courier]]: ''"What happened to Primm?"''
[[Johnson Nash]]: ''"Let's see. Been tough around here for a good while now. Worse since them thugs kidnapped our deputy. It started with that breakout from the prison up the road. First there was just a few thugs rolling through town, but then they got organized. Now they call themselves Powder Gangsters or something, and run around throwing dynamite and shooting people. Little while ago a good chunk of them left whatever kind of organization they got up there to squeeze all the food and drink out of us they could."''
([[PrimmJohnsonNash.txt|Johnson Nash's dialogue]]) The remaining residents holed up in the downtrodden Vikki & Vance Casino, resulting in a stalemate. While they had enough supplies and guns to last for a while and keep the convicts from getting inside to pick them off, they were in no position manpower-wise to retake the town.The [[Courier]]: ''"What's at Vikki and Vance?"''
[[Johnson Nash]]: ''"That's where we are. This here little casino brought some cash and bodies into the town before them Powder Gangsters came in. They can't rush us without eating a good bit of hot lead, but we are in kind of a box canyon. Guess this is as fitting a place for that as any. I reckon if they thought hard enough about it, they'd realize they got more bodies than we have bullets, but for now we're safe enough in here."''
([[PrimmJohnsonNash.txt|Johnson Nash's dialogue]]) Those lucky enough to reach the highway instead abandoned the town entirely, including the traders [[Samuel Kerr|Samuel]] and [[Michelle Kerr]] who cut their losses and re-established themselves at the [[188 Trading Post]] closer to New Vegas.The [[Courier]]: ''"Who are you?"''
[[Michelle Kerr]]: ''"Name's Michelle. My Dad and me run this store. His name's Samuel. I take the day shift and he takes nights. We came here about a month ago, when Primm went to hell on account of the prison break north of there. Found a bin to call home and set up shop."''
([[188Michelle.txt|Michelle Kerr's dialogue]])The [[Courier]]: ''"Why'd you leave Primm?"''
[[Samuel Kerr]]: ''"Michelle and I ran a little shop in Primm 'till a prison break north of town spoiled it for everyone. Goddamned convicts just about shut down I-15. When traffic dried up, we took to our heels to find us some customers. I'm not one to sit around waiting to get saved, and Michelle ain't, neither."''
([[188Samuel.txt|Samuel Kerr's dialogue]]) Over the next month, Primm became a lawless, penniless hell hole under convict control. The convicts keep a few of their number outside the Bison Steve Hotel patrolling the town, harassing and looting caravans coming up the I-15 to New Vegas. The Bison Steve itself was turned into their impromptu headquarters as the convicts plan to expand and wreck the town even further. The NCR maintains a token outpost at the eastern edge of town, manned by [[Hayes (Fallout: New Vegas)|Lieutenant Hayes]] with the [[1st Company]] of the [[5th Army Battalion]], keeping tabs on the convicts. The NCR considers the town a great strategic location in the southern Mojave, especially with the loss of Nipton, but Hayes laments that the Company is undermanned and outgunned in their plan to rout the convicts.The [[Courier]]: ''"Primm is in dire need of some real law."''
[[Hayes (Fallout: New Vegas)|Hayes]]: ''"We know Primm is a great strategic point, and we aren't blind to the needs of the town, but we're barely holding our own against the Powder Gangers. We don't have the guns or the personnel needed to carry out our mission, much less take on defending this town as well."''
([[PrimmCorporalHayes.txt|Hayes' dialogue]]) He states that just a single squad of reinforcements would be enough to tip the scales and allow his troopers to storm Primm and take it for the Republic, but has had no such luck with his requests back to the Mojave Outpost.The [[Courier]]: ''"What do you need to take over protecting the town?"''
[[Hayes (Fallout: New Vegas)|Hayes]]: ''"What we need, more than anything, is bodies. If we had just one more squad, we could easily install a sheriff and still handle our primary objective of protecting the interstate south of here. If you'd like to see the NCR include protection of Primm in its duties, then you'll have to get some more troops up here. Knight, at Mojave outpost, may be able to help."''
([[PrimmCorporalHayes.txt|Hayes' dialogue]]) ==Layout== Situated in the mid-to-southwestern area of the Mojave, the landscape of Primm is dominated by a few empty ranch homes, the rubble of the town's main streets and storefronts as well as a small NCR camp set up southwest of town. The outpost serves to prevent convicts from pushing further south to the NCR's Mojave outpost as opposed to protecting Primm, which has already fallen to the Powder Gangers. Most of the intact buildings of Primm are in the eastern section, which is completely surrounded by a metal fence. It is possible to engage the [[escaped convict]]s through the fence, but to enter the town proper will require approaching from the western or southern ends. When approaching the entrance to Primm, one will be greeted by an [[NCR trooper (Fallout: New Vegas)|NCR trooper]] warning that the center of town is held by convicts and a dangerous place to travel. An overpass outside of the town serves as a barricade between the convicts' territory and the NCR encampment. The derelict "El Diablo" roller coaster runs above and around the [[Bison Steve Hotel]]. Several convicts can be found on and around its tracks. Once inside the town, the Courier can access the Bison Steve Hotel, where [[Beagle|Deputy Beagle]] is being held by escaped convicts, or can cross the street to the [[Vikki and Vance Casino]], where the non-hostile citizens of Primm can be found. Either option will enable the Courier to trigger the quest [[My Kind of Town]], given by Deputy Beagle (in the Bison Steve Hotel) or [[Johnson Nash]] (in the Vikki and Vance Casino). In the southeast end of town, there are four [[Primm house|houses]]. Across the street from the Vikki and Vance Casino and the Bison Steve Hotel is the [[Nash residence]], which doubles as the [[Mojave Express]]. Inside this location, one can find [[ED-E]] on the table inside of the Nash residence. Once repaired, the quest [[ED-E My Love]] begins. Outside the Nash residence lies the remains of a courier, [[Daniel Wyand]]. There is a [[Campfire (Fallout: New Vegas)|campfire]] located southwest of the casinos, in the cluster of houses. To the northwest, behind the back wall and in front of the cliff, there is a [[Hollowed-out rock (Fallout: New Vegas)|hollowed-out rock]]. ==Buildings== {{columns|3| * [[Bison Steve Hotel]] * [[Deputy Beagle's residence]] * [[El Diablo rollercoaster]] * [[Nash residence]] * [[NCR tent]] * [[Primm house]] * [[Primm sheriff's office]] * [[Vikki and Vance Casino]] }} ==Inhabitants== {{columns|3| * [[Beagle|Deputy Beagle]] * [[Convict]]s * [[Daniel Wyand]] {{Icon|dead}} * [[ED-E]] * [[Hayes (Fallout: New Vegas)|Lieutenant Hayes]] * [[Johnson Nash]] * [[Layla (Fallout: New Vegas)|Layla]]1 * [[McBain (female)|Mrs. McBain]] {{Icon|dead}} * [[McBain (male)|Sheriff McBain]] {{Icon|dead}} * [[McGee|Sergeant McGee]] * [[NCR trooper (Fallout: New Vegas)|NCR trooper]]s * [[Old Laurie]] (formerly) * [[Primm Slim]] * [[Ruby Nash]] * [[Thug (Primm)|Thugs]]1 * [[Tyrone (Fallout: New Vegas)|Private Tyrone]] * [[Primm resident]]s * [[Vikki and Vance cashier]] * [[Vikki and Vance dealer]]s * [[Vikki and Vance floor manager]] * [[Michelle Kerr]] (formerly) * [[Samuel Kerr]] (formerly) * [[NCR trooper (Fallout: New Vegas)|NCR deputies]] {{Icon|cut}} * [[Powder Ganger deputy|Powder Ganger deputies]] {{Icon|cut}} }}''{{small|1During the unmarked quest [[A Team of Moronic Mercenaries]]}}'' ==Notable loot== * Two [[Sunset Sarsaparilla star bottle cap]]s - One is in the southeast house in the southern part of town, on top of a bookcase near the radio. These items will disappear after completing My Kind of Town. ==Related quests== {{columns|2| * [[Classic Inspiration]] * [[Don't Make a Beggar of Me]] * [[ED-E My Love]] * [[I Fought the Law]] * [[My Kind of Town]] * [[They Went That-a-Way]] * ''[[A Pair of Dead Desperados, I]]'' * ''[[A Team of Moronic Mercenaries]]'' * ''[[Big Winner, Vikki & Vance]]'' * ''[[Gland for Some Home Cooking]]'' }} ==Endings== {{Transcluded|Fallout: New Vegas endings}} {{transcludesection|article=Fallout: New Vegas endings|section=Primm|options=nointro}} ==Notes== * As of patch 1.02.3xx, citizens of Primm will reside in their houses during nighttime and wander around Primm during the daytime. * On the radio, [[Mr. New Vegas]] refers to Primm as "the other New Vegas." * If [[Meyers]] is chosen to be Primm's sheriff, followed by completing the endgame quest [[Eureka!]] for the NCR, he still remains as sheriff in the ending. * Primm is considered a "large" settlement although there are very few actual inhabitants. * One of the NCR troopers (the one without the helmet) always has an extra set of NCR armor in his inventory. * According to [[Primm Slim]], Primm is located in, or rather what used to be Clark County, Nevada. * The I-15, aka the "Long 15" which passes directly through Primm, has off-ramps from the highway in both directions. However, there are no on-ramps to return to the highway from the town. In addition, there are also no other road exits from the town. * When crossing the bridge into town across the overpass barricade, be wary of [[Frag mine (Fallout: New Vegas)|frag mines]] lying on or near the wooden boards that connect the bridge. Companions can often set off the mines due to the tight nature of the walkway. * {{cut}} Similar to [[Novac]], Primm would have had its own separate [[Fallout: New Vegas reputations|reputation]] meter, but this was [[Fallout: New Vegas cut content|cut]] during development. ==Appearances== Primm appears {{In|FNV}} and {{in|FOTV|noin}}. ==Behind the scenes== * The in-game Primm is based on the real-world town of [[Wikipedia:Primm, Nevada|Primm]] in [[Wikipedia:Clark County, Nevada|Clark County, Nevada]]. * During development, Primm became an area that drew on a significant amount of memory software, resulting in content having to be removed in patches to alleviate the risk of glitches and crashing, something [[Joshua Sawyer]] found regrettable.[https://youtu.be/0pLft_FQPFo?t=17077 ''Fallout: New Vegas'' 10th Anniversary Charity Stream (reference starts at 4:44:36)]
[[Joshua Sawyer]]: ''"'Why were the original convicts near the beginning of Primm removed with the updates?' I think it was memory. Primm was always a very memory-intensive area, and as we patched stuff... we had to remove stuff in patches. It sucked because it makes the areas feel more dead. It's why Increased Wasteland Spawns and mods like that really make everything feel more alive. But yeah, we had to remove a lot of that for memory."'' ==Bugs== * {{platforms|pc,ps3,xbox360}} If the New California Republic takes over Primm, some citizens will say that "Primm wimped out and accepted NCR rule." Even if Meyers or Primm Slim is chosen as Primm's sheriff, this line will be spoken from time to time throughout the wasteland and even from Primm residents. {{Verify|verified}} * {{platforms|ps3}} The dead courier outside the Mojave Express may not appear, therefore not allowing looting his body for his courier message. {{Verify|verified}} * {{platforms|pc}} The guard that's supposed to greet you may instead be hostile to you, regardless of your reputation or outfit. {{Verify|verified}} * {{platforms|ps3,xbox360}} The sheriff's duster inside the sheriff's office will not disappear after the My Kind of Town quest. {{Verify|verified}} ==Gallery== Primmlocalreal.jpg|Aerial overview FNV Vikki&Vance Casino.jpg|[[Vikki and Vance Casino]] Bison Steve hotel.jpg|[[Bison Steve Hotel]] Bison Steve rollercoaster.jpg|El Diablo, the Bison Steve roller coaster Nash residence.jpg|[[Nash residence]] NCR tent.jpg|[[NCR tent]]s FNV NCR flag Primm.jpg Primm sheriffs office.jpg|[[Primm sheriff's office]] Deputy Beagle's residence.jpg|[[Deputy Beagle's residence]] Primm house.jpg|[[Primm house]]s Primmbridge.jpg|Bridge that connects the east and west side Frag mines Primm.jpg|Armed [[Frag mine (Fallout: New Vegas)|frag mines]] FNV Jean Primm signage.jpg FNV Los Angeles Nipton street sign.jpg FNV Primm road sign.png FNV Billboard in game 2.jpg FNV loading billboard06.jpg FNV Loading screen death car.png FNV Primm roadsign render.png|Render of sign FNV Primm Nipton Vegas sign.png FNV Jean Primm LV road sign.png PrimmReputation.png|Reputation image The Innovator credits Primm.png|In the "[[The Innovator]]" credits {{icon|FOTV}} ==References== {{References}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group="Non-game"}} {{Navbox Primm}} {{Navbox locations FNV}} [[Category:Fallout: New Vegas locations]] [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]] [[Category:Primm| ]] [[de:Primm]] [[es:Primm]] [[fi:Primm]] [[fr:Primm]] [[it:Primm]] [[nl:Primm]] [[pl:Primm]] [[pt:Primm]] [[ru:Примм]] [[uk:Прімм]] [[zh:普瑞姆]]
Soviet satellite:
{{for|an overview of spacecraft|spacecraft}} {{Infobox location |games =FOTV |name =Soviet satellite |image =USSR Satellite TV.png |owners =[[Soviet Union]] (pre-War) |part of = }} The '''Soviet satellite''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}.[[Michael Emerson]]: ''"That set in the Nevada desert with the downed Soviet satellite, it was, when I walked out there and saw that we were going to be performing in the shadow of this amazing prop, God..."''
[[Jonathan Nolan]]: ''"That's Howard Cummings, our production designer, is just, just incredible."''
([https://ageofthenerd.com/2024/04/exploring-the-fallout-universe-an-interview-with-jonathan-nolan-and-michael-emerson "Exploring the Fallout Universe: An Interview with Jonathan Nolan and Michael Emerson" from Age of the Nerd]) ==Background== Originally built by the [[Soviet Union]] before the [[Great War]], it was launched into orbit around the Earth, though any functions it may have carried out during this time are unknown. The satellite is painted red and was powered by two solar panels. The bottom of the satellite housed what seems to be a sophisticated camera and communications system, indicating that it was built largely for surveillance purposes. The camera was a large red spherical structure with the Russian abbreviation "СССР" emblazoned onto it. Sometime after the bombs fell in 2077, the satellite underwent orbital reentry and suffered significant damage when it landed in the flat plains close to the ruins of [[Los Angeles International Airport]] in [[New California]] but remained mostly intact, with some parts of its machinery still clearly visible.{{FOTV|1|2}} ==In the TV series== ===[[The Target]]=== After escaping from [[the Ghoul]] in [[Filly]], [[Lucy MacLean]] attempts to escort [[Siggi Wilzig]] across the plains near the old airport, however, he was slowed due to an injured leg shoddily "repaired" with a [[Jim's Limbs]] prosthetic that was causing him to deteriorate from blood loss. At some point before they reached the site of the crashed satellite, Wilzig ingested a [[Plan D]] cyanide pill to hasten his demise. Once this fact was revealed, he implores Lucy to use his [[surgical Ripper]] and remove his head containing the [[cold fusion]] artifact in order to carry it the rest of the way to [[Lee Moldaver|Moldaver]] before passing away. After initial reluctance, Lucy performs the surgical removal and leaves the headless body propped up against the old satellite, where it is later found by the Ghoul who was following after [[CX404]] and her canine nose detecting Wilzig's scent. ===[[The Head]]=== Wilzig's corpse and the satellite are visited for a third time by [[Thaddeus]] and [[Maximus]] (disguised as [[Titus|Knight Titus]]) who discern that the artifact they were sent to find for the [[Brotherhood of Steel]] is embedded in the deceased's head, sending them after Lucy and the Ghoul. ==Appearances== The Soviet satellite appears {{in|FOTV}} [[Fallout TV series episodes|episode]]s "[[The Target]]" and "[[The Head]]." ==Behind the scenes== The appearance of the Soviet satellite in the ''Fallout'' TV series is the second occurrence of post-[[Divergence]] Soviet technology in the [[canon]] of the [[Fallout series|''Fallout'' series]], after the [[Assault rifle (Fallout)|AK-112 assault rifle]] in the ''[[Fallout]]'' video game. A special encounter in ''[[Fallout Tactics]]'' involved discovering the [[Mir]] space station but there is no in-universe evidence of its ownership past its name; after the whole of ''Fallout Tactics'' was declared non-canon and eventually transitioned into dubious canon, it no longer qualifies. ==Gallery== FOTV s1 ep2 LAX.png|Lucy and Wilzig approach the satellite FOTV Soviet satellite.png|The Ghoul and CX404 investigate Sovietsatelliteclose.png|Closeup ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Fallout TV series}} {{Navbox spacecraft}} {{Navbox vehicles}} [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]] [[Category:Satellites]] [[Category:Soviet Union]] [[de:Sowjetischer Satellit]] [[ru:Разбившийся советский спутник]]

The '''BBQ Shack''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}.

==Background==
Formerly a business establishment in the pre-[[Great War|War]] era in the former city of [[Santa Monica]], [[State#California|California]], sometime after the destruction of the [[New California Republic|NCR]] capital of [[Shady Sands]] in [[Timeline#2283|2283]], [[Sorrel Booker]] formed an organization of his own out of a self-righteous mission to restore order in [[Los Angeles]], naming it [[Govermint|the Govermint]] with himself as its president and claimed the old restaurant as their headquarters. From here, they conduct their operations including sending [[Sheriff (TV series)|"sheriffs"]] to collect tribute paid to them by those they secure under their protection rackets including the organ-harvesters [[Huey]] and [[Squirrel (TV series)|Squirrel]] out of a nearby [[Super Duper Mart (TV series)|Super Duper Mart]] outlet.

Booker's crew also seemingly maintains a small farm close to the building, raising [[hog]]s to slaughter for meat to feed themselves as well as utilizing the animals as low-tech body disposal if the need arises.

===Wanted posters===
[[File:Govermint wanted posters.png|thumb|250px|Wanted posters]]
While the legitimacy of the Govermint's bounties is questionable, the BBQ Shack's wall features an assortment of bounty posters for valuable targets, with notable ones including [[Lee Moldaver]], at least one [[Super mutant (TV series)|super mutant]], and a couple of [[ghoul]]s by [[Timeline#2w96|2296]].
{{clear}}

==In the TV series==
===[[The Trap]]===
[[File:Sorrel Booker.png|thumb|250px|Govermint "president" [[Sorrel Booker]], current owner of the BBQ Shack]]
After being picked up by sheriffs of the Govermint at the destroyed Super Duper Mart following the deaths of their clients Huey and Squirrel [[The Ghouls|a short time prior]], [[the Ghoul]] is brought to their HQ at the BBQ Shack and re-introduced to Govermint president Sorrel Booker, who recognizes the mutant bounty hunter from a past encounter and mentions his lifelong quest for "[[Janey Howard|her]]," but is brushed off by the Ghoul who instead focuses on using a needle and thread to reattach the finger previously bitten off by [[Lucy MacLean]].<ref name="FOTV0106">Events of {{FOTV|1|6}}</ref>

As Booker begins to chastise his former associate for supposedly disrupting the Govermint's business by destroying the organ harvesting operation, the Ghoul taunts him and [[Troy (TV series)|Sheriff Troy]] to whom he claims he killed the man's father during [[The Target|a shootout]] in [[Filly]], escalating Troy's anger further until Booker diffuses the tension and orders his men to take their guest out and feed him to the hogs. However, when Troy attempts to grab the Ghoul, the bounty hunter retaliates and swiftly disarms the Govermint lackey along with [[Rex (TV series)|Sheriff Rex]], and both are gunned down by the Ghoul, to Booker's chagrin. The Ghoul is momentarily distracted from dealing with Booker when he notices the shack's selection of wanted posters, particularly the one of Lee Moldaver whom he recognizes, but instead by her name "Miss Williams" when he met her centuries ago, before the bombs.<ref name="FOTV0106">Events of {{FOTV|1|6}}</ref>

'''Westside Medical Clinic''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] in [[Los Angeles]] {{in|FOTV}}.

==Background==
The medical clinic was built in the [[Hollywood]] district of [[Los Angeles]], [[State#California|California]], situated along a section of the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame]].

By the 23rd century, the desert sands and rolling winds of the [[wasteland]] have resulted in the interior being half-buried but still accessible.

==In the TV series==
===[[The Ghouls]]===
During the trek from [[Hollywood Boulevard]] to a [[Super Duper Mart (TV series)|Super Duper Mart]] near [[Santa Monica Boulevard]], [[the Ghoul]] and [[Lucy MacLean]] pass near the Westside Medical Clinic and overhear someone shouting inside. Lucy enters at gunpoint ahead of the Ghoul, where they discover [[Roger (TV series)|Roger]], another [[ghoul]] squatting in one of the rooms, furiously shouting his name as he is on the verge of [[Feral ghoul|going feral]].

After Roger tries to get the Ghoul to share his supply of [[inhaler vial]]s only to be told he does not have any, he resigns himself to his fate, lamenting that he had managed to persevere for decades since first showing symptoms and remarking that the Ghoul himself will likely outlast the rest of them. The Ghoul helps ease Roger by getting him to remember the taste of pre-War food like [[BlamCo Mac & Cheese]], ice cream, and apple pie. Just as Roger thinks fondly on his mother's cooking, he is executed with a headshot by the Ghoul, to Lucy's shock.

As the Ghoul loots the body of his friend for valuables and then begins harvesting his teeth and flesh for "[[ass jerky]]," he asks Lucy for her name and ponders when she reveals her last name of "MacLean." After a few retorts over the Vault dweller's insistence about her mission to rescue [[Hank MacLean|her father]], the Ghoul's last insult causes Lucy to question why he continues in such a violent lifestyle which confuses and angers the bounty hunter. He then forces Lucy to finish carving up Roger's body before they leave to continue their journey.

==Appearances==
The Westside Medical Clinic appears only {{In|FOTV}} [[Fallout TV series episodes|episode]] "[[The Ghouls]]."

The '''Hollywood Sign''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}.

==Background==
The Hollywood Sign was originally erected in 1923 on Mount Lee near the [[Hollywood]] district in [[Los Angeles]] [[State#California|California]], where it initially spelled out "Hollywoodland" until later being shortened to "Hollywood." Since then, it became recognized as an iconic symbol of the district's global fame as an American entertainment hub. At some point in the 21st century, the [[Nuka-Cola Corporation]] secured sponsorship of the sign in return for the construction of a giant neon sign reading "Sponsored by Nuka-Cola" erected just below the sign itself.

The Hollywood Sign and its corporate-sponsored subtitle lasted intact through the [[Great War]] and 219 years of exposure to the elements and wear and tear, with the electrical systems for its lighting rig remaining intact as well.

==In the TV series==
===[[The Beginning]]===
In [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]], shortly after [[Lee Moldaver]] activates her [[cold fusion]] reactor at [[Griffith Observatory]] to restore power to the ruins of Los Angeles, the resulting surge of electrical power reaches the Hollywood sign just after [[Lucy MacLean]], [[the Ghoul]], and [[CX404]] exit an escape tunnel into [[Hollywood Forever]], showing off the sign as still being intact as well as the name of its long-defunct corporate sponsorship.<ref>{{FOTV|1|8}}</ref>

During the [[First Battle of Hoover Dam]] against [[Caesar's Legion]] coming east across the [[Colorado River]], Camp Golf was on the frontlines and saw heavy action but ultimately continued to survive after the Legion's defeat. By [[Timeline#2281|2281]], due to the bulk of the NCR forces being moved to garrison the [[Hoover Dam]] for the impending [[Second Battle of Hoover Dam]], the resort has been left in the hands of the [[New California Republic Rangers]] led by [[Hanlon|Chief Hanlon]] as their regional HQ, serving as both a communications and quartermaster hub. [[Super mutant (TV series)|Super mutant]] (corpse) |robots =[[Eyebot (TV series)|Eyebot]] }} The '''Enclave research colony'''{{Ref|(Note)}} is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== Built before the [[Great War]],"2076" is [[:File:FOTV Enclave research colony 05.png|shown]] on the wall while CX404 runs on the treadmill. the facility has managed to remain under the control of the [[Enclave]] by [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]] in spite of multiple failures and defeats suffered by the organization since the mid-23rd century. Enclave experiments seen in the facility include behavioral engineering (using selectively bred dogs in which sub-standard newborns are immediately incinerated), biological research (with captives held in a train car designed for handling live cargo), and energy production via [[nuclear fusion]].Events of {{FOTV|1|2}} The facility seems to be crucial to some form of overarching Enclave experiment intended to be tested on the surface, with the [[Vault]]s themselves supposedly secondary to whatever this experiment is.[[Lucy MacLean]]: ''"I need you to tell me what you were really doing here."''
[[Hank MacLean]]: ''"And then?"''
Lucy: ''"And then I'm gonna turn you into the father I thought you were. You lied to me my whole life."''
Hank: ''"I know that's how you feel. You think this is the real world. The surface is the experiment. Not the Vaults."''
Lucy: ''"What experiment?"''
Hank: ''"I've already sent my R&D out into the wasteland. Their Boxes are the latest models, too. So you can't even see them. Unbeknownst to everyone, they're following orders written for them centuries ago."''
({{FOTV|2|8}}) The facility had a communications network which connected it to several [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]] assets and facilities on the West Coast, including the [[Vault-Tec headquarters (TV series)|Vault-Tec headquarters]] in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]]; a [[Las Vegas management Vault|management Vault]] built under [[Las Vegas]], [[Nevada]]; and [[Vault 33]] in [[Santa Monica]], California via a Pip-Boy kept by Enclave asset [[Hank MacLean]].{{FOTV|2|8}}: This Pip-Boy is seen inside Hank's keepsakes box, and Steph Harper uses it to contact the Enclave at this facility. Its communications infrastructure also seemingly allowed it to listen on many other radio frequencies used throughout the wasteland.[[Steph Harper]]: ''"This is Stephanie Harper. Hank MacLean's wife. I don't know how this works, exactly, but he said that you were always listening, and... If you can hear this... initiate Phase 2."''
({{FOTV|2|8}}){{FOTV|2|8}}: When the Enclave colony is shown and the messages from Hank and Norm are played, many other overlapping voices and messages, many of which are not directed to the Enclave or to anyone in particular, are heard. In 2296, the facility received word from [[Steph Harper]], the wife of Hank MacLean, to begin Phase Two of this experiment. It is unclear what specifically Phase Two entails, but it is suggested that it involves the [[Forced Evolutionary Virus]] and the populations of some Vaults, including [[Vault 32|Vaults 32]] and 33.[[Ronnie McCurtry|Ronnie]]: ''"Hey, boss. Now that we've found food, it's time for phase two?"''
[[Norm MacLean]]: ''"What is your name?"''
Ronnie: ''"Oh, um, I'm Ronnie. McCurtry."''
Norm MacLean: ''"I decide the next steps up here, Ronnie."''
Ronnie: ''"I know, yeah, you're the-- you're the boss. I know you call the shots. Just thought I'd introduce myself, 'cause I was Bud's personal assistant."''
Norm MacLean: ''"Hm, so?"''
Ronnie: ''"So, uh, let's just say I was the guy who took the lunch orders when Bud was meeting with the Vault investors. 'Future Enterprise Ventures'? The whole plan for Vaults 32 and 33?"''
Norm MacLean: ''"What do you know about that?"''
Ronnie: ''"Like I said, I was just the guy who got the lunch orders, but I do know that Phase 2 was very important to the experiment."''
({{FOTV|2|4}}) {{Small|In "[[The Wrangler]]," "Future Enterprise Ventures" is explicitly confirmed to be a cryptonym of "Forced Evolutionary Virus," and these "investors" are confirmed by [[Robert House]] in "[[The Strip]]" to be the Enclave.}}{{FOTV|2|5}} ==In the TV series== ===[[The Target]]=== At an unspecified point in time, Enclave scientists study and measure the weight of newborn puppies bred in the facility, with the ones falling under the minimum 10 ounces being thrown into an incinerator. [[Siggi Wilzig]], one of the scientists, weighs a particular puppy designated [[CX404]] and seemingly has a change of heart upon seeing her, as he secretly alters the weight scale to show her meeting the minimum weight requirement and takes her on as his test subject. As he is leading her to his private lab, they stop as scientists pass by a [[Enclave soldier (TV series)|guard]] checkpoint wheeling a gurney with the corpse of a [[Super mutant (TV series)|super mutant]] on it. As time passes, Wilzig nurtures the growing CX404 in his lab in secret while working on a project involving a pre-War [[cold fusion]] device once owned by the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]]. Sometime around 2296, as Wilzig prepares to leave the facility to bring the device to his benefactor [[Lee Moldaver]] in [[New California]], he and CX404 are discovered by an [[Enclave administrator|administrator]] who gets into a scuffle with Wilzig before pushing him away and activating an alarm, only to be mauled to death by the canine defending her master immediately after. Trying to make a quick escape, Wilzig and CX404 navigate through the facility and exit onto the exterior surface level. They are discovered by an automated turret that fires upon them as they flee from the facility but are able to get away unharmed. Despite its secretive nature, the facts of Wilzig's flight from the facility, his Enclave ties, the artifact he brought with him, and his destination are uncovered by members of the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 4)|Commonwealth Brotherhood of Steel]]. They later issue the mission to locate Wilzig and recover the artifact to the [[Knights of San Fernando]], a Brotherhood chapter active in the [[Los Angeles]] area. ===[[The Strip]]=== [[Steph Harper]], cornered by angry [[Vault 32 dweller]]s after [[Chet (TV series)|Chet]] revealed her to be a pre-War [[Canada|Canadian]], uses an Enclave Pip-Boy which Hank kept stored in his keepsake box to call the Enclave facility via an emergency frequency, telling them to begin Phase 2 of their experiment. These details are received by the Enclave facility, where several scientists and guards are seen walking around, along with a single [[Eyebot (TV series)|Eyebot]], in the atrium. Steph's message is shown being transcribed on a terminal labeled as Commstation 4, which registers the message as a request to initiate Phase 2. After this, a full exterior view of the facility is shown, revealing it to be a set of two buildings on either side of a gorge in a snowy, mountainous area, connected by several bridges. Many other communications are heard, including undirected requests for help, but also Hank MacLean's message from the Vault-Tec facility in Las Vegas (as heard in "The Innovator") and Norm's message from the Los Angeles Vault-Tec headquarters (as heard in "The Handoff,") revealing that the Enclave at the facility have been listening in on everyone. ==Layout== The exterior structure of the colony is a non-descript warehouse complex in an unspecified snowy, mountainous region. The building's most distinguishing feature is the large, glass-covered roof. Behind its walls, the majority of the facility is underground, with the surface portion merely the crown of a vast underground storage facility. Seemingly stretching across eight stories, the facility is built around a 200-meter-long atrium used for loading and unloading freight trains. Staggered loading balconies and a cargo crane remain present, although they have since been repurposed by the facility for research. ==Personnel== * [[Siggi Wilzig]] (formerly) * [[Enclave administrator]] * [[Enclave scientist (TV series)|Enclave scientists]] * [[Enclave soldier (TV series)|Enclave soldiers]] ==Appearances== The Enclave research colony appears {{in|FOTV}}. {{FOTV appearances|2=102|16=208}} ==Behind the scenes== * {{Note|(Note)}} The name of the facility is never stated in the show's [[Fallout TV series season 1|first season]]. The '''Mojave Mission School''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] in the [[Mojave Wasteland]] in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]].

==In the TV series==
===[[The Other Player]]===
The [[hooded super mutant]] brings the Ghoul here when the Ghoul wants continue the search for his family alone. At some point later, Maximus and [[Thaddeus]] are led here by [[CX404|Dogmeat]], allowing them the opportunity to come to an agreement with the Ghoul.

==Appearances==
The Mojave Mission School appears only in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]].

("[[The Trap]]") ===Arrival of Lucy and Maximus=== [[File:The Past Vault 4.png|250px|thumb|Lucy and Maximus arriving in Vault 4]] In [[Timeline#2296|2296]], after [[Maximus]] was shot in the arm by a cannibal, [[Lucy MacLean]] takes him into [[Hawthorne Medical Laboratories]] to find medical supplies. However, they are trapped and dropped down the hatch originally used by the Hawthornes to lure in wastelanders. After coming to, they find themselves in Vault 4, where the doctor treats Maximus' wounds and are quarantined for a short time before being introduced to the Vault at large, seemingly expected to stay long-term. While Lucy is relieved to be in a Vault again, Maximus is unnerved by how eerily happy everyone seems, warning Lucy that the Vault inhabitants might be a cult. Lucy did not find anything wrong until [[Benjamin (TV series)|Overseer Benjamin]] greeted them, and she noticed [[Nose Edmundson|Dr. "Nose" Edmundson]] and [[Powell|Nurse Powell]], bearing visible mutations. Lucy's subsequent meeting with Overseer Benjamin and discussing the Vault's open policy ended on a sour note; after Benjamin's tactless joke about the nuking of Shady Sands, she inquired about level 12 and the instructions to stay out of it, leading to Benjamin politely throwing her out of his office. After witnessing the ritual for Shady Sands and [[Lee Moldaver]]'s likeness, she resolved to investigate level 12. Maximus had a different path, particularly after Birdie offered him the spare unit 428, complete with a hot shower and a basket full of consumables. To a wastelander who never had either, it was the moment he resolved to stay and refused to go with Lucy to break the one rule they were given. Taking advantage of the Vault's lax security, Lucy easily gained access to level 12, discovering remnants of Vault 4's original science experiments. After watching an undated experiment tape showing the horrific gulper birth and the cryo pods holding test subjects the new Vault dwellers were unable to save, she concluded that the mutated denizens were responsible for the atrocities. This led to a confrontation when Dr. Edmundson arrived to investigate the open doors, believing it to be a containment breach. Injuring the doctor with a beaker of acid, Lucy was caught by dwellers arriving to deal with the containment breach. In the subsequent trial in the atrium, the whole story was explained to Lucy. Despite her ignorance of either Vault 4's story or the experiment at [[Vault 33]], she was condemned and put on trial. The decision was made to put her to death, by banishing her to the surface with two weeks' worth of supplies. The elaborate banishment ritual involved a dull execution sword, one factor that led Maximus to erroneously believe the dwellers were trying to kill Lucy. Stealing the power plant's [[Fusion core (TV series)|fusion core]] to power up his [[T-60 power armor (TV series)|T-60 power armor]] (recovered by the foraging parties), he interrupted the "execution," injuring several dwellers before Lucy intervened.[[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'']], "[[The Radio]]" Despite the incident, no further consequences were imposed, aside from banishing them both to the surface. The dwellers did not risk recovering the fusion core, even though backup power would only last a few days.[[Lucy MacLean]]: ''"Well, without their fusion core, their auxiliary power will only last a few days, and... and then what?"''
("[[The Radio]]") Rather than doom the Vault, Lucy persuaded Maximus to return the core and abandon the T-60, which they did by simply dumping it down the trapdoor at Hawthorne Medical, with the elated Vault 4 dweller assigned to scrub the capture room thanking them up the chute. ==Layout== [[File:FOTV Hawthorne Medical Laboratories.png|thumb|250px|The [[Hawthorne Medical Laboratories]] building]] Vault 4 is located beneath [[Hawthorne Medical Laboratories]], with the main bunker housing the entrance on a nearby plain, completely desertified by 2296. The Hawthorne building is connected to the Vault via a chute located inside the building, repurposed as a trap, luring in people with the promise of medical supplies.[[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'']], "[[The Past]]" [[File:Vault4atrium.jpg|thumb|250px|The atrium full of greenery]] The actual Vault is identified as model 96JQ1164, twelve levels deep (all numbered except for level 1, the surface, identified as G or Ground), with the dominant feature being the atrium, a large communal space three floors high, used for social gatherings, meals and other activities requiring the participation of the entire Vault. It is designed for 200 inhabitants, with each family provided a living unit in one of the "neighborhoods" (discrete living quarter areas named, e.g. Sycamore Street) that can accommodate two adults and two children in comfort, protected by three feet (~92 cm) of lead casing and earth covering. The units are standard designs shared with [[Vault 33]] and others, fitted with all the modern amenities. [[File:Vault4overseer.jpg|thumb|250px|Lucy and Benjamin in the overseer's office]] The overseer's office overlooks the atrium, like in many other Vaults, and other facilities used on a daily basis connect to it, such as the classroom. Vault dwellers are free to move around the Vault and access even sensitive areas, including the fusion power plant. The only area that is off-limits is level 12, where the laboratories used by the original scientist contingent are located, including the genetic research laboratory filled with leftovers of their unethical research, and the cryo suspension tubes, some still occupied.[[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'']], "[[The Trap]]" Vault 4 is mentioned as having only one foosball table, and the Vault's washrooms are said to be confusing for newcomers to use.[[Benjamin]]: ''"Oh, and we only have one foosball table, so if you want to play, you got to sign up. If there's no pencil on the sign-up sheet, please let me know. I do have pencils. Uh, oh, and if you're unfamiliar with how the bathrooms work, just ask. Asking is less embarrassing than getting it wrong. Trust me. We've had incident after incident with newcomers."'' ("[[The Trap]]") ==Appearances== Vault 4 appears {{In|FOTV}} [[Fallout TV series episodes|episodes]] "[[The Past]]," "[[The Trap]]" and "[[The Radio]]." ==Behind the scenes== * The chalkboard in the episode includes a timeline of events for the New California Republic, which placed the Fall of Shady Sands in 2277. Confusion in the community led some to decide that it meant ''Fallout: New Vegas'' never happened in the show timeline. [[Todd Howard]] clarified in an interview with IGN the following week that this is not the case: {{Quotation|“And we talked through it, and it was, ‘This would be a pretty impactful story moment that a lot of things anchor on,"' Howard says. But for anyone confused about how the city could be blown up by the time the show takes place, Howard explains that all the timeline details should line up. “We’re careful about the timeline,” he says. “There might be a little bit of confusion in some places. But everything that happened in the previous games, including New Vegas, happened. We’re very careful about that.” “All I can say is we’re threading it tighter there, but the '''bombs fall just after the events of New Vegas.'''”|[https://www.ign.com/articles/fallout-official-timeline-confirmed-how-the-show-fits-in-with-the-games IGN]}} [[File:FOTV Vault 4 Classroom BTS.jpg|thumb|200x200px|The behind-the-scenes photograph of the classroom in Vault 4.]] * In "[[The World of Fallout]]," a promotional website for [[Fallout TV series season 2|season 2]] of the TV series, a behind-the-scenes photo of the Vault 4 classroom shows a different version of the chalkboard timeline. In place of "The Fall of Shady Sands" in 2277, this version depicts an event titled "The Fall" in 2291. * Vault 4 was first shown in a video used at the ''Fallout'' display at CCXP 2023 in Sao Paulo, Brazil. The full video is presently unavailable anywhere online, but segments of it can be seen [https://www.youtube.com/shorts/4JUzMAW58Ck here]. * Vault 4 is shown to be connected to the [[Hawthorne Medical Laboratories]] building. This could suggest that Vault is located in Hawthorne, California, a city in L.A. County; however, the company is more likely named after the Hawthornes, the Vault-Tec scientists who ran Vault 4. [[Brotherhood of Steel]] (2296) |map marker = }} {{Quotation|Property of Area 51, return if found|Written on the [[Alien Ship]]}} '''Area 51''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== Pre-[[Great War|War]], Area 51 was a military garrison for the [[United States Air Force]]. It housed research facilities studying captured [[alien]] technology, including a [[flying saucer]]. The vessel was later retaken by its alien crew, but ended up crashing somewhere within [[State#California|California]] where it remained well into the 23rd century by 2161.[[PRO SCEN.MSG (Fallout)]]: ''"{40000}{}{Dome}"''
''"{40001}{}{You find a small label that reads: 'Property of Area-51. Return if found.'}"'' By late 2077, other artifacts stored in its warehouses included a preserved [[Zetan|Zetan corpse]], various pieces of alien technology including a [[shock baton]], [[Alien blaster (Fallout 3)|alien blaster]], and [[UFO]], a copy of the [[Constitution of the United States]], an artifact resembling the Ark of the Covenant, a [[Terracotta Army]] soldier, and a [[Holy Hand Grenade]]. The facility's location within the deserts of the West Coast inspired military engineers to create an array of wind turbines around its perimeter, powered by a fusion generator, that could rapidly clear away large sand deposits in minutes (similar to the [[DERVISH camouflage system]] utilized by the [[Hidden Valley bunker|bunkers]] of [[Hidden Valley]]). When not in use, the turbines themselves are housed within underground silos to preserve them. After the nuclear apocalypse, a number of [[Zetan]] aliens that had been held captive within the facility escaped and retreated to [[Skull Canyon]].''[[Fallout: The Roleplaying Game]]'' scenario ''[[Showdown in Skull Canyon]]'', pp. 4, 16. At some point, the rolling sands and desert winds of the [[wasteland]] buried much of the pre-War structures under an immense layer of sand, but the power control tower for the wind turbine array (housed in a fake playground rocket structure) was left exposed and accessible. ==In the TV series== ===[[The Golden Rule]]=== Sometime after the [[Battle of Griffith Observatory]] in [[Timeline#2296|2296]], the [[Knights of San Fernando]] uncovered the location of Area 51 and decided on claiming it as their new headquarters. After [[Maximus]] and his squad of knights obtained a pre-War holodisk which [[Quintus|Elder Cleric Quintus]] called the "key" to Area 51, a sizable number of the San Fernando chapter traveled to the pre-War military base on board the ''[[Caswennan]]''. On-site at the fake playground structure, a pair of scribes used a [[Fusion core (TV series)|fusion core]] to power the ground console, in conjunction with another scribe who plugged in the key to a console on the ''Caswennan''{{'}}s flight deck, to reactivate the wind turbines and clear away the years of sand built-up that managed to keep much of Area 51 preserved. After exploring the central warehouse and recovering a substantial number of pre-War artifacts and weaponry, Area 51 became the new base of the chapter. It later served as the site of Quintus' meeting with the other elders of the [[Grand Canyon Brotherhood of Steel|Grand Canyon]], [[Coronado Brotherhood of Steel|Coronado]], and [[Yosemite Brotherhood of Steel|Yosemite]] chapters to begin planning for a civil war with the [[Commonwealth Brotherhood of Steel|Commonwealth Brotherhood]] with the intent of shifting the axis of power within the wider Brotherhood back to the West Coast.{{FOTV|2|2}} ===[[The Profligate]]=== {{Section|FOTV}} ==Appearances== [[File:FO1AlienSaucer.png|thumb|The [[Alien Ship]], a special encounter in ''[[Fallout]]'']] Area 51 appears only {{In|FOTV}} [[Fallout TV series episodes|episode]]s "[[The Golden Rule]]" and "[[The Profligate]]." It is mentioned in ''[[Fallout]]'', as a print on a flying saucer in the [[Alien Ship]] [[Fallout special encounters|special encounter]]. It was intended to appear in ''[[Fallout 2]]'', inhabited by a group of scientists, but was [[Fallout 2 cut content|cut]] from the final version of the game.[[Fallout 2 Official Strategies & Secrets]], p. 335: ''"A second set of drafts hypothesized the army of the Master (from ''Fallout 1'') roaming the wastes in a huge, armored land fortress, scooping up muties to use as slave labor. As you can see, neither of these stories made their way into the final game. Although some parts of them did—Lynette's head, for example, was once going to be the spokesperson for a group of scientists living in the ruins of a base in Area 51."'' It is also mentioned in ''[[Showdown in Skull Canyon]]'', a scenario for ''[[Fallout: The Roleplaying Game]].'' ==Behind the scenes== * Area 51 is based on the real world Groom Lake Facility, code named [[wikipedia:Area 51|Area 51]]. It is located within the Nevada Test and Training Range. The base is used by the United States military to develop and test many top secret aircraft and weapons technology, though it has long been a source of speculation among conspiracy theorists. Many theories involve captured aliens and their technology, hence why the location is mentioned on a crashed alien ship in ''Fallout''. * In an early draft of ''Fallout 2'', [[Joanne Lynette]]'s talking head was supposed to be used for a spokesperson for a group of scientists living in the ruins of Area 51. However, this never made it into the game. * For ''Fallout 2'', [[Chris Avellone]] also entertained the possibility of an Area 51 location consisting of nothing but the set for a fake moon landing.[https://www.watchoutforfireballs.com/61e ''Watch Out for Fireballs!'', Extrasode: Fallout 2 (Part 2) - Feat. Chris Avellone] * Area 51 was never planned for inclusion in ''[[Fallout: New Vegas]]'' from the start.Question: ''Was Big MT made because you weren't able to use Area 51? BROTHERHOOD BASE - DAY (102.20)"'' - [[The End script|"The End" script]], p. 29 ==History== ===Background=== A remote pre-[[Great War|War]] airport on the West Coast, the facility was taken over by the [[Knights of San Fernando]] chapter of the [[Brotherhood of Steel]] sometime before [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]].''"The middle of fucking nowhere. The remains of a hangar and runway tell us this place was once an airport."'' - [[The End script|"The End" script]], p. 30. It has since served a pivotal role in the Brotherhood's operations in and around [[New California]], acting as a training camp for the Brotherhood's countless aspirants. ===The End=== The area is introduced alongside the character of Maximus as other initiates are beating him by a set of bunker entrances before scattering. Many areas of the airbase are seen, including the runway, watchtower, barracks, and main hangars. Maximus is sentenced to latrine duty and exhibits extreme anger and frustration. Later during an engineering lesson in a hangar, the class is interrupted, with the aspirants running outside to see the arrival of [[The Prydwen|the ''Prydwen'']] and a squad of knights from the Eastern Brotherhood in T-60 armor. Maximus and Dane later sneak off to get an up-close look at one of the suits being stored in the garage. ===The Beginning=== {{Section|FOTV}} ==Layout== The base's layout includes extensive runways, hangars, barracks, and command facilities. Large swaths of tarmac allow Brotherhood [[Vertibird]]s to take off and land safely. A watchtower overlooks the runway and is also used by younger Brotherhood initiates to smoke. Initiates are seen clearing pathways, suggesting that the Brotherhood had recently taken the airbase, or are in the middle of restoring or expanding it. The base is also home to a large underground bunker complex, with at least nine separate partially submerged bunker entrances being visible adjacent to the airfield. Brotherhood of Steel members can be seen building what looks to be roadways between the bunkers and the rest of the base. By the 2290s, it was one of the Brotherhood's known strongholds on the West Coast. It is home to a sizable contingent of the organization's forces, including clerics, officers, support personnel, and a large number of aspirants of all ages. These aspirants and hopefuls are housed in the base's barracks section, which contains at least 23 barracks buildings and some medical tents. The buildings in the area appear to be built post-war, as fresh wood can be seen and there is no sign of dilapidated condition. From here, the recruits undergo training from [[clerics]] to become active field soldiers of the Brotherhood. The bunkhouses held both males and females together. Dane recovered in a tented clinic area close to the barracks after they were injured. One of the hangars was used by the clerics to teach classes on old-world technology for aspirants, utilizing desks and chalkboards. They punished wrong answers using a switch. A garage was used to store power armor suits at stations for the arriving Eastern Brotherhood knights. An old airplane was used as a meeting place between Elder Cleric Quintus and Maximus under the suspicion he had purposefully injured his friend Dane. Another building was used as an armory for all types of weapons. ==Notes== The pre-War [[Flag of the United States|American flag]] can be seen still being flown at the airbase, alongside the Brotherhood flag, despite the Brotherhood largely viewing the former USA as a failed nation in previous ''Fallout'' media. ==Behind the scenes== [[File:FNV Nellis AFB poster Keeping America Safe.png|thumb|right|x200px|"Keeping America Safe!"]] * The scenes for the Brotherhood airbase were filmed at [[wikipedia:Wendover Air Force Base|Wendover Airport]] in [[Utah]], formerly known as Wendover Air Force Base until 1969. The base prominently served as the training site of the [[wikipedia:509th Composite Group|509th Composite Group]], the B-29 unit that carried out the [[wikipedia:Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki|atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki]] during [[Wikipedia:World War II|World War II]]. The locations used for filming include: ** Ordnance storage area, where [[Maximus]] receives a beat-down from [[Thaddeus]] and his [[Thaddeus' minion|minions]]. The western part of the area is also used to depict latrine digging. ** The control tower, base headquarters, and operations building are next to hangar #1. ** Airmen dormitories are in the northeastern part of the base (with two tents set up in front of the dining hall, housing communications equipment, and the infirmary). ** Parked [[Vehicles in the Fallout TV series|C-123 and staff car]] next to the squadron hangar, in the scene where Maximus is interrogated by Cleric [[Quintus]]. ** The buildings at the western part of the ordnance storage area, currently used by the [https://clui.org/clui-locations/clui-wendover/points-interest-around-old-wendover-airfield/clui-wendover Center for Land Use Interpretation]. * The hangar at the airbase features a poster that heavily resembles the [[Nellis Air Force Base]] "Keeping America Safe!" [[Poster (Fallout: New Vegas)|poster]] from [[Fallout: New Vegas loading screens|loading screens]] {{In|FNV}}. The same text can be seen on the bottom of the poster, and text can also be seen on the top of the poster. '''Santa Monica Pier''' was a pre-War attraction in [[Los Angeles|Los Angeles County]], [[California]] which appears {{in|FOTV}}.

==Background==
Located in [[Santa Monica]], California, Santa Monica Pier was a popular tourist attraction which included a small amusement park (with a Ferris wheel and roller coasters), concession stands, and areas for viewing the [[Pacific Ocean]]. The entrance to [[Vault 33]] was built just slightly further inland from the pier.

As of 2296, much of the pier up to its Ferris wheel is still standing, but the sections further past have collapsed into the ocean. Save for some scattered buildings and the now-exposed entrance of Vault 33, most of the surrounding area has been desertified, with little remaining of the urban ruins of Santa Monica proper.

==Appearances==
The Santa Monica Pier appears {{in|FOTV}}, in the episode "[[The End (episode)|The End]]" and its end credits. It also appears in a pre-War flashback in the episode "[[The Innovator]]." The corresponding area is also visible on the [[Fallout map|first ''Fallout'' game's world map]].

==Behind the scenes==
The Santa Monica Pier was filmed at [[wikipedia:Elizabeth Bay|Elizabeth Bay, Namibia]], a ghost town and former diamond mine. Visual effects were used to add the pier's Ferris wheel and roller coaster, as well as the Malibu Mountains in the background, but everything else in the shots was practical.<ref>[https://archive.ph/A5p5K Los Angeles Times: "In ‘Fallout,’ a destroyed L.A. comes to life, with some help from ... Namibia?"]</ref>

[[Huey]] and [[Squirrel (TV series)|Squirrel]] (2296) }} The '''Super Duper Mart''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== One of many franchise locations across the [[United States of America|United States]] owned by the pre-[[Great War|War]] [[Super-Duper Mart (company)|Super-Duper Mart]] company, this particular store is located in [[Santa Monica]] in [[Los Angeles]] County, [[State#California|California]]. The bombs dropping in [[Timeline#2077|2077]] spared much of the building itself, though it was seemingly looted of much of its inventory by scavengers over the years. Sometime prior to [[Timeline#2296|2296]], the abandoned building was taken over by wastelanders [[Huey]] and [[Squirrel (TV series)|Squirrel]] and set up as a "legitimate" business selling medical supplies including [[inhaler vial]]s. To accrue a supply of the vials, they also entered into the market of organ-harvesting by hiring [[bounty hunter]]s to capture [[ghoul]] and human wastelanders alike, relying on a repurposed [[Mister Handy (TV series)|Mister Handy]] unit, [[Snip Snip]], to perform the crude surgical operations. At some point, [[Sorrel Booker]]'s [[Govermint]] secured Huey and Squirrel's operation under a protection racket, involving the occasional visit by Govermint "[[Sheriff (TV series)|sheriffs]]" to collect their cut of the profits while handling any troublemakers that could disrupt business. ==In the TV series== ===[[The Ghouls]]=== [[The Ghoul]] escorts a captive [[Lucy MacLean]] across the wasteland from [[Hollywood Boulevard]] to the Super Duper Mart in order to sell her to the organ-harvesters in exchange for a resupply of inhaler vials after losing them to the [[Gulper (TV series)|gulper]]. Shortly after Lucy enters the fortified building, he collapses outside from withdrawal.Events of {{FOTV|1|4}} Lucy is greeted by Snip Snip in the supermarket lobby and led to Huey and Squirrel who send them to the medical room, meanwhile as she notices the several ghouls they have locked up. Lucy tries to plead her case but is astonished when the Mister Handy offers to restore her missing finger, previously cut off by the Ghoul. Lucy's relief to have not been sold into sex slavery is then squashed when Snip Snip reveals she is instead going to have her organs harvested, right before he tranquilizes her. After awakening on Snip Snip's operating table, Lucy manages to free herself before his buzzsaw can cut her too deep, then evades his attacks long enough to obtain and use an old defibrillator to fry his circuits. She then augments his tranq-gun arm and loads it with projectiles filled with [[Abraxodyne Chemical]] industrial cleaner to make acid darts. She brings the robot to the lounge and threatens Huey and Squirrel to release their captives. They initially comply and let out some of the ghouls, including [[Freed ghoul|one]] who thanks Lucy before leaving. When she notices another, [[Martha (TV series)|Martha]] still in her cell as well as some others, she demands their release, then fires a dart near the harvesters when they prove reluctant and try to warn her about the danger. Lucy finds out too late that the remaining ghouls she had released have turned feral. She quickly retreats as they charge forward, knocking over Snip Snip and attacking Huey and Squirrel. The two only manage to kill one before Squirrel is tackled and mauled by a second, followed by Huey taking down that one but failing to stop the third from tearing out his throat right before getting a mutual kill. As Lucy looks over the carnage, she finds Martha approaching her and starting to turn feral. Just as the ghoul gives in and attacks, Lucy arms herself with a [[10mm pistol (TV series)|10mm pistol]] and puts Martha down, to her own regret. The [[Vault 33]] dweller later emerges from the Super Duper Mart outfitted in a set of leather armor and discovers the incapacitated bounty hunter. Though she admits that she may end up becoming a mutant like him, she firmly states she will never become a cruel and heartless monster like him, providing a supply of inhaler vials before leaving. Rejuvenated, the Ghoul enters the ravaged supermarket and indulges in the harvesters' alcohol and drug supplies including taking more of the inhaler vials. He then discovers a holotape copy of ''[[The Man from Deadhorse]]'' and out of curiosity, plays it on the nearby [[Radiation King]] television set, becoming lost in memories of his former life as Cooper Howard in the era before the bombs. ===[[The Trap]]=== Sometime after Lucy's departure from the Super Duper Mart, the Ghoul is awoken by the arrival of men in sheriffs' uniforms who extract Snip Snip's fusion core and place him under arrest for allegedly disrupting a "legitimate" business protected by the "government." Under sheriff escort, the bounty hunter is taken from the Super Duper Mart to the [[BBQ Shack (TV series)|BBQ Shack]].Events of {{FOTV|1|6}} ==Layout== The Super Duper Mart in Santa Monica is located close to several ruined high-rises and is within walking distance of a massive impact crater left by a nuclear explosion. Potential transactions are directly made through an old speaker located outside the entrance. The building still has power by 2296, with working lighting displays and pre-War music being played on the speakers. The old commercial refrigerators in the store were repurposed as holding cells for captives waiting to have their organs harvested, with the locks controlled by a console operated by Huey and Squirrel, who typically reside in a lounge area in the center of the store where they mostly watched old holotapes on a TV and let Snip Snip handle most of the day to day work. A kids play area is also advertised within the store with small rides, and much of the store still retains the [[Halloween]] decorations that went up before the bombs. The Mister Handy primarily conducts his surgical operations in what appears to be the former store clinic. Despite the grisly outcome of his operations, Snip Snip still obeys some of his old healthcare programming and maintains a supply of medical equipment which he will use to mend injuries on wastelanders brought in, such as a drawer of multiple severed fingers to sew on in place of lost ones. The actual organ-harvesting takes places in a separate room repurposed as an operating theater. ==Appearances== The Santa Monica Super Duper Mart appears {{In|FOTV}} episodes "[[The Ghouls]]" and "[[The Trap]]." ==Behind the scenes== Scenes set in the Super Duper Mart were filmed around July to August 2022 at an empty ShopRite outlet redesigned with the fictional supermarket's signs and logo, located at 2424 Hylan Boulevard in Staten Island, New York. ==Gallery== FOTV Super Duper Mart crater.png|Across a crater in Los Angeles FOTV Super Duper Mart yard.png|The entrance yard of the building FOTV1-4 Daytripper.jpg|Bottles of [[Day Tripper|Daytripper]] seen on a countertop inside FOTV leaked set photo SDM July 2022.jpg|Leaked set photo from July 2022 ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Fallout TV series}} [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]] [[Category:Super-Duper Mart locations]] [[ru:Супермаркет (телесериал)]] [[zh:大无敌超市(电视剧)]]

The '''Shady Sands courthouse''' is a building in [[Shady Sands]] that briefly appears in flashbacks {{in|FOTV}}. 

==Background==
The heart of the capital's judiciary, the courthouse was a Greek Revival two-story building located in the historic square of Shady Sands, near the pillar dating back to the earliest days of the settlement. It was characteristic of its red brick and oversized NCR flag permanently hanging above the front entrance. Near the courthouse was a Shady Sands tram system station, with a field of corn nearby (as agriculture continued to flourish in the town, even after it became a capital).<ref>{{fotv|1|8}}</ref>

Destroyed in the nuclear attack that vaporized the capital, a part of the courthouse survived: Its cupola fell to the bottom of the crater, remaining there ever since.<ref>{{fotv|1|5}}</ref>

==Appearances==
The Shady Sands courthouse appears {{In|FOTV}} [[Fallout TV series episodes|episodes]] "[[The Past]]", "[[The Trap]]", and "[[The Beginning]]".

The '''Fabulous New Vegas sign''' is an [[Fallout: New Vegas locations#Unmarked individual locations|unmarked location]] in the [[Mojave Wasteland]] {{In|FNV}}. It also appears {{in|FOTV}}.

==Layout==
The location is situated north of the main entrance to [[Camp McCarran]], close to the southern wall of the [[New Vegas Strip|Strip]].

==Notes==
* As suggested by its appearance in the [[Fallout: New Vegas intro|cinematic intro]] in which an [[NCR Veteran Ranger]] with an [[Anti-materiel rifle (Fallout: New Vegas)|anti-materiel rifle]] snipes a [[Fiends|Fiend]] by the [[El Rey Motel]], the sign does have a platform on the rear face of it. However, this platform is inaccessible to the player character by normal means, nor does any NPC ever use it as in the intro.
* In ''Fallout: New Vegas'', the sign was altered so that "New" covers the former name "Las" as well as the "e" in "New" actually being a number "3" reversed. There is also a smiley face painted in the "o" in "Welcome."

==Appearances==
The Fabulous New Vegas sign appears {{In|FNV}}, in the [[Fallout 4 holotape games|Pip-Boy minigame]] ''[[Atomic Command (Fallout 4)|Atomic Command]]'' {{In|FO4}} and {{in|FOTV}}.

==Behind the scenes==
* The in-game Fabulous New Vegas sign is based on the real-world [[Wikipedia:Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas sign|Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas sign]], which is located in [[wikipedia:Paradise, Nevada|Paradise, Nevada]].
* A physical recreation of the ''Fabulous New Vegas'' version of the sign was displayed at gaming conventions to promote ''Fallout: New Vegas''{{'}}s release in 2010.
* In the ''Fallout'' TV series, the sign first appeared in the credits for the [[Fallout TV series season 1|season 1]] episode "[[The Beginning]]." Prior to the release of [[Fallout TV series season 2|season 2]], a poster was released depicting the main characters underneath the sign.
** There are some slight differences with the sign in the TV series compared to how it appears in ''Fallout: New Vegas''. At the bottom of the sign, there is a sliver of plastic remaining from the pre-War sign that is not present in ''Fallout: New Vegas''. It features the logo and name of the real-world company [[wikipedia:YESCO|YESCO]], which owns and maintains the sign in real life. The text for "NEVADA" is white in ''Fallout: New Vegas'', but in the show, it has been darkened to more closely resemble its dark blue appearance in real life. Additionally, the end of the "D" is visible in ''Fallout: New Vegas'', but it is not visible on the poster, having been further worn away. In contrast to its ''Fallout: New Vegas'' appearance, the red star at the top of the sign in the TV series' current depiction is undamaged.

The '''Uranium City Internment Camp''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{in|FOTV}}.

==Background==
Before the [[Great War]], this internment camp was operated by the [[United States Armed Forces]] to detain Canadian citizens during or after the [[United States annexation of Canada]]. Military personnel, including [[United States Marine Corps|U.S. Marines]], were used in controlling the population of the camp. 

At some point, a mass escape occurred at the camp, seemingly due to an attack by Canadian partisans.

==In the TV series==
===[[The Handoff]]===
[[Steph Harper]] and [[Joan (TV series)|her mother]] escape from the internment camp along with other Canadians. They are chased by guards who fire at them. Steph and her mother are discovered by a [[Vertibird (TV series)|Vertibird]] and a Marine in power armor who tells them to return to the camp or he will shoot, while using the slur "Hoser" to describe them. Before either party can react, a [[Canadian rebel|suicide bomber]] kills the soldier, although Steph's mother is mortally wounded. She tells Steph to get south and survive, while telling her not to worry if she harms anyone to do so, as she shouldn't think of them as human beings, but Americans.

==Appearances==
The Uranium City Internment Camp appears only {{In|FOTV}} [[Fallout TV series episodes|episode]] "[[The Handoff]]."

==Behind the scenes==
[[wikipedia:Uranium City|Uranium City]] is a real-world community in northern Saskatchewan, Canada. It was originally founded in the 1950s to house workers of nearby uranium mines.
